name: Essential (Primary) Hypertension
treatment: Lifestyle first (weight loss ≥5%, DASH diet, salt <5 g/day, exercise 150 min/week, limit alcohol, quit smoking). Drugs for Stage 2 (≥140/90) or Stage 1 (130–139/80–89) with high CV risk, diabetes or CKD; target <130/80 (2025 AHA/ACC). Start two-drug single-pill combination if BP ≥20/10 above target.
medications: Telmisartan 40–80 mg OD or Losartan 50–100 mg OD
Chlorthalidone 12.5–25 mg OD or Indapamide 1.5 mg SR OD. Resistant HTN: add Spironolactone 25–50 mg OD.
precautions: Do not combine ACEi + ARB. Check K⁺ and creatinine 1–2 weeks after starting ACEi/ARB/spironolactone. ACEi/ARB contraindicated in pregnancy. Avoid NSAIDs. Rise slowly (orthostatic hypotension in elderly).

name: Hypertensive Emergency
treatment: BP >180/120 with acute target-organ damage. ICU admission; reduce MAP by no more than 25% in first hour, then to 160/100 over 2–6 h, then normal over 24–48 h (exceptions: aortic dissection SBP <120 within 20 min; ischemic stroke specific targets).
medications: IV Labetalol 20 mg bolus then 20–80 mg q10min (max 300 mg) or infusion 1–2 mg/min
Nicardipine 5 mg/h, titrate 2.5 mg/h q5–15min (max 15 mg/h)
precautions: Avoid sublingual nifedipine (precipitous drop → stroke/MI). Avoid beta-blockers alone in cocaine toxicity. Nitroprusside → cyanide toxicity with prolonged use/renal failure.

name: Stable Angina / Chronic Coronary Syndrome
treatment: Risk-factor control, antianginal therapy, antiplatelet + high-intensity statin; revascularization (PCI/CABG) for refractory symptoms or high-risk anatomy.
medications: Atorvastatin 40–80 mg OD or Rosuvastatin 20–40 mg OD
Metoprolol succinate 25–200 mg OD or Bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg OD
Ezetimibe 10 mg if LDL above target.
precautions: No nitrates within 24 h of sildenafil (48 h tadalafil). Avoid non-dihydropyridine CCB with beta-blocker in heart failure/bradycardia. Seek emergency care if rest pain >20 min.

name: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
treatment: Emergency reperfusion: primary PCI within 90–120 min of first medical contact; fibrinolysis within 30 min if PCI unavailable within 120 min. Oxygen only if SpO₂ <90%.
medications: Aspirin 162–325 mg chewed then 75–100 mg OD
P2Y12: Ticagrelor 180 mg load then 90 mg BD or Prasugrel 60 mg then 10 mg OD (or Clopidogrel 600 mg load)
precautions: Rule out dissection before anticoagulation/thrombolysis. Avoid nitrates in RV infarct, hypotension, PDE5 use. Prasugrel contraindicated with prior stroke/TIA. Watch arrhythmias and mechanical complications.

name: NSTEMI / Unstable Angina
treatment: Antiplatelet + anticoagulation, anti-ischemic therapy, risk stratification (GRACE score); early invasive strategy (<24 h) for high risk, immediate (<2 h) for very high risk.
medications: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC OD or Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD
investigations: serial hs-troponin (0/1 h or 0/2 h algorithm)
precautions: Dose-adjust enoxaparin in renal impairment. Dual antiplatelet therapy typically 12 months — balance bleeding risk; add PPI if GI risk.

name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)
treatment: Four-pillar guideline-directed medical therapy, diuretics for congestion, device therapy (ICD/CRT) when EF ≤35% despite therapy, salt restriction, cardiac rehab.
medications: Bisoprolol 1.25–10 mg OD, Carvedilol 3.125–25 mg BD or Metoprolol succinate
Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD or Empagliflozin 10 mg OD
Ivabradine, hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in selected patients.
precautions: Monitor K⁺/creatinine. 36-hour washout between ACEi and sacubitril/valsartan (angioedema). Avoid NSAIDs, non-DHP CCBs, thiazolidinediones. Daily weights; IV iron if ferritin <100.

name: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
treatment: Diuretics for congestion, SGLT2 inhibitor, control BP, AF, obesity, diabetes; exercise training.
medications: Empagliflozin 10 mg OD or Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD
Finerenone (2024 FINEARTS-HF evidence) in selected patients
investigations: amyloid workup (technetium pyrophosphate scan, serum free light chains) where suspected.
precautions: Avoid over-diuresis (preload dependent). Check renal function and potassium with MRAs.

name: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure / Acute Pulmonary Edema
treatment: Sit upright, oxygen/non-invasive ventilation (CPAP/BiPAP) if hypoxic, IV loop diuretics, vasodilators if BP adequate; inotropes if cardiogenic shock. Treat precipitant.
medications: Dobutamine 2–20 mcg/kg/min or Norepinephrine in shock
precautions: Monitor urine output, electrolytes (hypokalemia), creatinine. Avoid nitrates in severe aortic stenosis/hypotension.

name: Atrial Fibrillation
treatment: Rate or rhythm control, stroke prevention by CHA₂DS₂-VA score, treat risk factors (alcohol, OSA, obesity, HTN). Urgent cardioversion if unstable; catheter ablation for symptomatic patients.
medications: Rate: Metoprolol 25–100 mg BD, Bisoprolol, Diltiazem 60–120 mg TDS

Digoxin 0.125–0.25 mg OD. Rhythm: Amiodarone, Flecainide (no structural disease), Dronedarone. Anticoagulation: Apixaban 5 mg BD (2.5 mg BD if 2 of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, creatinine ≥1.5), Rivaroxaban 20 mg OD with food, Dabigatran 150 mg BD
Warfarin (INR 2–3) for mechanical valve/moderate–severe mitral stenosis.
investigations: TEE before cardioversion if AF >48 h without 3 weeks anticoagulation.
precautions: DOACs contraindicated with mechanical valves. Adjust for renal function. Avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF (WPW). Amiodarone → thyroid, liver, lung, eye toxicity.

name: Atrial Flutter
treatment: Similar to AF: rate control, anticoagulation by stroke risk; cavotricuspid isthmus ablation is first-line definitive therapy (>90% success).
investigations: ECG (sawtooth flutter waves, 2:1 block at ~150 bpm)
precautions: Class IC drugs without AV-nodal blockers may cause 1:1 conduction. Anticoagulate before cardioversion as for AF.

name: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (AVNRT/AVRT)
treatment: Vagal manoeuvres (modified Valsalva), then adenosine; synchronized cardioversion if unstable; catheter ablation for recurrent episodes.
medications: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push, then 12 mg (repeat 12 mg once)
precautions: Adenosine contraindicated in severe asthma; warn of transient chest discomfort. Avoid verapamil in broad-complex tachycardia or WPW with AF.

name: Ventricular Tachycardia
treatment: Pulseless → ACLS defibrillation. Unstable with pulse → synchronized cardioversion. Stable → antiarrhythmic. ICD for secondary prevention; ablation for recurrent VT.
medications: Amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min then 1 mg/min × 6 h, 0.5 mg/min × 18 h
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV for torsades
precautions: Treat as VT if in doubt. Avoid QT-prolonging drugs. Correct K⁺ >4.0 and Mg²⁺ >2.0.

name: Ventricular Fibrillation / Cardiac Arrest
treatment: High-quality CPR (100–120/min, 5–6 cm depth), early defibrillation, ACLS algorithm, airway, treat reversible causes (4 Hs & 4 Ts), post-arrest care with temperature control, coronary angiography.
medications: Amiodarone 300 mg IV after 3rd shock, then 150 mg
precautions: Minimize interruptions in compressions (<10 s). Avoid hyperventilation and hyperoxia post-ROSC.

name: Sinus Bradycardia / Sick Sinus Syndrome
treatment: Asymptomatic → observe. Symptomatic → stop offending drugs, atropine, pacing; permanent pacemaker for symptomatic sinus node dysfunction.
medications: Atropine 1 mg IV q3–5 min (max 3 mg)
Dopamine 5–20 mcg/kg/min or Epinephrine 2–10 mcg/min infusion
precautions: Atropine ineffective in heart transplant and infranodal blocks. Review all rate-slowing drugs.

name: Complete (Third-degree) Heart Block
treatment: Temporary transcutaneous/transvenous pacing if unstable, then permanent dual-chamber pacemaker. Treat reversible causes (inferior MI, Lyme, drugs, hyperkalemia).
medications: Atropine 1 mg IV (often ineffective), Isoprenaline infusion, Dopamine or Epinephrine as bridge.
precautions: Avoid AV-nodal blocking agents. Monitor for asystole; keep pacing pads on.

name: Wolff–Parkinson–White Syndrome
treatment: Catheter ablation of accessory pathway is curative. Acute orthodromic AVRT: vagal manoeuvres/adenosine. Pre-excited AF: procainamide or cardioversion.
medications: Flecainide/Propafenone long-term if ablation not possible.
precautions: Never give adenosine, digoxin, verapamil, diltiazem or beta-blockers in pre-excited AF (risk of VF).

name: Long QT Syndrome
treatment: Beta-blockade, avoid QT-prolonging drugs, correct electrolytes; ICD for cardiac arrest survivors/high risk; left cardiac sympathetic denervation.
medications: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV for torsades
precautions: Check crediblemeds.org list before prescribing (macrolides, fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics, ondansetron). Avoid sudden loud noises/swimming per genotype.

name: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
treatment: Beta-blocker/non-DHP CCB for symptoms; cardiac myosin inhibitor for obstructive HCM; septal myectomy/alcohol septal ablation for refractory obstruction; ICD for high SCD risk.
precautions: Avoid dehydration, vasodilators, nitrates and high-dose diuretics in obstruction. Avoid competitive strenuous sport until assessed. Mavacamten: REMS-type EF monitoring, CYP interactions.

name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
treatment: As HFrEF GDMT; treat cause (alcohol, viral, peripartum, tachycardia-induced); ICD/CRT; heart transplant/LVAD for end stage.
medications: anticoagulation if AF or LV thrombus.
precautions: Strict alcohol abstinence; avoid cardiotoxic drugs (anthracyclines, trastuzumab without monitoring).

name: Acute Pericarditis
treatment: NSAID + colchicine, rest from strenuous activity until resolution; treat cause.
medications: Ibuprofen 600–800 mg TDS or Aspirin 750–1000 mg TDS for 1–2 weeks then taper
Colchicine 0.5 mg BD (0.5 mg OD if <70 kg) for 3 months
Prednisone low dose only if NSAID contraindicated.
precautions: Avoid steroids as first line (increase recurrence). Avoid NSAIDs post-MI (use aspirin). Restrict sport 3 months in myopericarditis.

name: Pericardial Effusion / Cardiac Tamponade
treatment: Tamponade → urgent echo-guided pericardiocentesis; IV fluids temporarily. Treat underlying cause. Pericardial window for recurrent effusions.
medications: cause-specific (NSAID/colchicine, antitubercular therapy, chemotherapy for malignant effusion).
investigations: pericardial fluid analysis (cell count, ADA, cytology, culture).
precautions: Avoid diuretics, vasodilators and positive-pressure ventilation in tamponade.

name: Constrictive Pericarditis
treatment: Diuretics for congestion; anti-inflammatory therapy for transient constriction; pericardiectomy for chronic constriction; antitubercular therapy if TB.
precautions: Over-diuresis worsens output. TB is a leading cause in India/Africa — screen.

name: Acute Myocarditis
treatment: Supportive care, heart failure therapy, arrhythmia management; mechanical support in fulminant cases; immunosuppression for giant-cell/eosinophilic/sarcoid myocarditis.
medications: Corticosteroids ± other immunosuppressants for specific histology.
precautions: Avoid NSAIDs in myocarditis (unlike pericarditis). Avoid competitive sport for 3–6 months.

name: Infective Endocarditis
treatment: Prolonged IV bactericidal antibiotics (4–6 weeks), surgery for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, large vegetations with emboli.
medications: Empirical (native valve): Ampicillin + (Flucloxacillin or Cefazolin) + Gentamicin, or Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h + Gentamicin if MRSA risk. Strep viridans: Penicillin G 12–18 MU/day or Ceftriaxone 2 g OD × 4 weeks. MSSA: Flucloxacillin 2 g q4h or Cefazolin. Enterococcus: Ampicillin + Ceftriaxone.
investigations: ≥3 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics
precautions: Monitor vancomycin/gentamicin levels and renal function, audiometry. Dental hygiene; prophylaxis before dental procedures for prosthetic valves/prior IE.

name: Acute Rheumatic Fever
treatment: Eradicate streptococci, anti-inflammatory therapy, bed rest in carditis, secondary prophylaxis.
medications: Benzathine penicillin G 1.2 MU IM single dose (or Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg OD × 10 days)
Haloperidol/Valproate for chorea. Prophylaxis: Benzathine penicillin every 3–4 weeks (5–10 years or to age 40 with RHD).
precautions: Avoid aspirin in viral illness in children (Reye syndrome) — monitor. Penicillin allergy → erythromycin/azithromycin.

name: Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
treatment: Rate control, anticoagulation if AF, diuretics; percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy for favourable anatomy; surgical repair/replacement otherwise. Secondary penicillin prophylaxis.
medications: Beta-blockers or Ivabradine (slows HR, prolongs diastole)
Warfarin INR 2–3 if AF/thrombus (DOACs not recommended in moderate-severe MS)
precautions: Pregnancy is high risk — counsel. Avoid tachycardia.

name: Aortic Stenosis
treatment: Watchful waiting if asymptomatic; aortic valve replacement (TAVI or SAVR) when severe and symptomatic or EF <50%.
medications: No drug alters progression. Cautious diuretics
investigations: Echo (AVA <1.0 cm², mean gradient >40 mmHg, Vmax >4 m/s)
precautions: Avoid vasodilators/nitrates and dehydration in severe AS. Syncope/angina/dyspnea → urgent referral.

name: Aortic Regurgitation
treatment: Treat cause; vasodilators for hypertension; surgery if symptomatic, LVEF ≤55% or LV end-systolic dimension >50 mm.
medications: ACEi/ARB or Dihydropyridine CCB (Nifedipine) for BP
precautions: Acute severe AR (dissection/endocarditis) is a surgical emergency. Avoid bradycardia-inducing drugs in chronic AR.

name: Mitral Regurgitation
treatment: Primary MR: surgical repair if symptomatic or LV dysfunction. Secondary MR: optimize HF therapy, CRT, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
precautions: Acute MR after MI (papillary muscle rupture) → emergency surgery.

name: Mitral Valve Prolapse
treatment: Reassurance; beta-blockers for palpitations; surgery if severe MR.
medications: Propranolol 10–40 mg TDS or Metoprolol for palpitations/chest pain.
precautions: Monitor with periodic echo; endocarditis prophylaxis not routinely needed.

name: Aortic Dissection
treatment: Type A → emergency surgery. Type B uncomplicated → medical (anti-impulse) therapy; complicated → TEVAR.
medications: IV Esmolol (500 mcg/kg bolus then 50–300 mcg/kg/min) or Labetalol to HR <60 and SBP 100–120 mmHg within 20 min
precautions: Never thrombolyse. Beta-block before vasodilator (avoid reflex tachycardia).

name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
treatment: Surveillance for small AAA; elective repair (open or EVAR) at ≥5.5 cm men/≥5.0 cm women or growth >1 cm/year; emergency repair if rupture.
medications: smoking cessation (no drug slows growth reliably).
investigations: Abdominal USG (screening men 65–75 who ever smoked)
precautions: Ruptured AAA — permissive hypotension (SBP 70–90) before repair. Avoid fluoroquinolones (possible aneurysm risk).

name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
treatment: Smoking cessation, supervised exercise, risk-factor control, revascularization for critical limb ischemia or lifestyle-limiting claudication.
medications: Aspirin 75–100 mg or Clopidogrel 75 mg OD
Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD + aspirin (COMPASS) in selected
precautions: Cilostazol contraindicated in heart failure. Foot care; avoid tight footwear.

name: Acute Limb Ischemia
treatment: Immediate heparin, urgent vascular surgery (embolectomy, catheter-directed thrombolysis, bypass); fasciotomy for compartment syndrome; amputation if non-viable.
medications: Unfractionated heparin 80 U/kg bolus then 18 U/kg/h
precautions: "6 Ps": treat within 6 h. Watch reperfusion hyperkalemia and myoglobinuria.

name: Deep Vein Thrombosis
treatment: Anticoagulation ≥3 months (provoked) or extended (unprovoked/cancer); compression for symptoms; catheter thrombolysis for limb-threatening DVT.
medications: Apixaban 10 mg BD × 7 days then 5 mg BD
Rivaroxaban 15 mg BD × 21 days then 20 mg OD
Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD (bridge to warfarin INR 2–3 or dabigatran)
precautions: Avoid DOACs in antiphospholipid syndrome (triple positive), pregnancy, severe renal impairment. Watch bleeding.

name: Pulmonary Embolism
treatment: Anticoagulation; systemic thrombolysis for high-risk (shock); catheter-directed therapy for intermediate-high risk deteriorating; IVC filter if anticoagulation contraindicated.
medications: LMWH or UFH (UFH if thrombolysis likely)
Alteplase 100 mg IV over 2 h for massive PE.
precautions: Do not delay anticoagulation if high suspicion. Thrombolysis contraindications: recent surgery, stroke, bleeding.

name: Varicose Veins / Chronic Venous Insufficiency
treatment: Compression stockings, leg elevation, exercise, weight loss; endovenous laser/radiofrequency ablation, sclerotherapy, surgery.
medications: Micronized purified flavonoid fraction (Diosmin-hesperidin) 1000 mg/day for symptoms
precautions: Do not apply compression if ABI <0.8 (arterial disease). Skin care to prevent ulcers.

name: Superficial Thrombophlebitis
treatment: Warm compress, compression, NSAIDs; anticoagulation if ≥5 cm length or near saphenofemoral junction.
medications: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC OD × 45 days for extensive thrombosis.
precautions: Within 3 cm of SFJ → treat as DVT.

name: Dyslipidemia (Hypercholesterolemia)
treatment: Diet (reduce saturated/trans fat), exercise, weight loss; statin intensity according to ASCVD risk; LDL targets <55 mg/dL very high risk, <70 high risk, <100 moderate.
medications: Atorvastatin 10–80 mg OD, Rosuvastatin 5–40 mg OD
PCSK9 inhibitors (Evolocumab 140 mg SC q2w, Alirocumab), Inclisiran 284 mg SC at 0, 3 months then 6-monthly
precautions: Statins contraindicated in pregnancy. Check for myopathy; avoid simvastatin with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Check LFT at baseline.

name: Hypertriglyceridemia
treatment: Restrict alcohol, refined carbohydrates; weight loss; glycemic control; TG >500–1000 mg/dL → reduce pancreatitis risk urgently (very-low-fat diet).
medications: Omega-3 fatty acids (icosapent ethyl 2 g BD)
insulin infusion ± plasmapheresis in TG-induced pancreatitis.
precautions: Fibrate + statin → myopathy risk (avoid gemfibrozil with statins). Adjust fenofibrate in renal impairment. --- # 2. Respiratory

name: Bronchial Asthma
treatment: Stepwise GINA approach. Preferred track: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (Steps 1–2), maintenance and reliever therapy (MART) at Steps 3–4, add-on LAMA/biologics at Step 5. Avoid SABA-only therapy. Inhaler technique, trigger avoidance, action plan.
medications: Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg 1 puff PRN (max 12/day) or 1–2 puffs BD as MART
Biologics (Omalizumab, Mepolizumab, Benralizumab, Dupilumab, Tezepelumab) for severe asthma.
investigations: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility (≥12% and 200 mL FEV₁)
precautions: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers and aspirin/NSAIDs in aspirin-exacerbated disease. Rinse mouth after ICS (thrush). Montelukast → neuropsychiatric warning.

name: Acute Severe Asthma (Status Asthmaticus)
treatment: Oxygen to SpO₂ 93–95%, repeated bronchodilators, systemic steroids, IV magnesium; ICU/intubation if exhaustion, silent chest, rising CO₂.
medications: Salbutamol 2.5–5 mg nebulized every 20 min × 3 (or continuous)
Prednisolone 40–50 mg PO or Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV q6h × 5–7 days
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 20 min
precautions: Sedatives contraindicated outside ICU. Monitor potassium. Normal PaCO₂ in a breathless asthmatic = impending failure.

name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
treatment: Smoking cessation, vaccination (influenza, pneumococcal, RSV, Tdap), pulmonary rehabilitation, bronchodilators per GOLD group, long-term oxygen if PaO₂ ≤55 mmHg, NIV for chronic hypercapnia.
medications: add ICS (triple therapy) if eosinophils ≥300 or frequent exacerbations
Azithromycin 250 mg OD/500 mg 3×/week for exacerbators
precautions: Oxygen target 88–92% (risk of CO₂ retention). ICS increases pneumonia risk. Azithromycin → QT prolongation, hearing loss.

name: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
treatment: Controlled oxygen, short-acting bronchodilators, systemic steroids, antibiotics if increased sputum purulence; NIV for acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis (pH <7.35).
medications: Antibiotics 5 days: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 625 mg TDS, Doxycycline 100 mg BD or Azithromycin
precautions: Target SpO₂ 88–92%; monitor glucose on steroids.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
treatment: Severity by CURB-65/PSI; outpatient vs inpatient vs ICU; antibiotics 5 days minimum (until afebrile 48 h and stable); oxygen, fluids.
medications: Outpatient healthy: Amoxicillin 1 g TDS or Doxycycline 100 mg BD (or macrolide if low resistance). Comorbid: Amoxicillin-clavulanate + Azithromycin, or Levofloxacin 750 mg OD. Inpatient: Ceftriaxone 1–2 g OD + Azithromycin 500 mg OD. Severe/ICU: Ceftriaxone + Azithromycin (or + respiratory fluoroquinolone)
add Vancomycin/Linezolid for MRSA, Piperacillin-tazobactam for Pseudomonas risk
precautions: Fluoroquinolones mask TB — avoid as first line in TB-endemic regions without TB testing. Macrolide/FQ → QT prolongation.

name: Hospital-Acquired & Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
treatment: Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics based on local antibiogram and MDR risk; de-escalate with cultures; 7 days usually.
medications: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h, Cefepime 2 g q8h or Meropenem 1 g q8h
add Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h or Linezolid 600 mg BD for MRSA
second anti-pseudomonal agent (Amikacin) if high risk
precautions: Head-of-bed elevation 30–45°, daily sedation holds, oral care. Monitor renal function with vancomycin/aminoglycosides/colistin.

name: Aspiration Pneumonia / Lung Abscess
treatment: Antibiotics, postural drainage, treat dysphagia/dental disease; percutaneous drainage/surgery for non-resolving abscess.
medications: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2 g IV TDS or Ampicillin-sulbactam
precautions: Aspiration pneumonitis (chemical) often needs no antibiotics initially. Nil by mouth until swallow evaluated.

name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Drug-Susceptible)
treatment: Directly observed/supported therapy under national programme (NTEP in India). Standard 6-month regimen 2HRZE/4HR; 4-month HPZM regimen (isoniazid, rifapentine, pyrazinamide, moxifloxacin) for ≥12 years per 2025 ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA and WHO; 4-month 2HRZ(E)/2HR for children with non-severe TB.
medications: Weight-band fixed-dose combinations: Isoniazid 5 mg/kg, Rifampicin 10 mg/kg, Pyrazinamide 25 mg/kg, Ethambutol 15 mg/kg daily
investigations: CBNAAT/Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (also detects rifampicin resistance)
precautions: Hepatotoxicity (H, R, Z) — monitor LFT; stop if ALT >3× with symptoms or >5×. Rifampicin reduces OCP, warfarin, ART efficacy; turns urine orange. Ethambutol → optic neuritis. Notify cases.

name: Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB)
treatment: Specialist centre; 6-month all-oral BPaLM (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for ≥14 years with fluoroquinolone-susceptible RR-TB; BPaL if fluoroquinolone-resistant; WHO 2025 alternatives include BDLLfxC; longer individualized regimens otherwise.
medications: Bedaquiline 400 mg OD × 2 weeks then 200 mg 3×/week
Moxifloxacin 400 mg OD — all for 26 weeks.
precautions: QT prolongation (bedaquiline + moxifloxacin), linezolid → anemia, thrombocytopenia, peripheral/optic neuropathy, lactic acidosis. Contact tracing.

name: Latent Tuberculosis Infection
treatment: TB preventive therapy for household contacts, PLHIV, before biologics/transplant, silicosis, dialysis.
medications: 3HP: Isoniazid 900 mg + Rifapentine 900 mg weekly × 12 weeks
investigations: CXR and symptom screen to exclude active TB
precautions: Rule out active disease first (avoid monotherapy resistance). Rifamycin drug interactions.

name: Bronchiectasis
treatment: Airway clearance (physiotherapy, devices), treat exacerbations, treat cause, vaccination; long-term macrolide for ≥3 exacerbations/year; Pseudomonas eradication.
medications: Exacerbation 14 days: Amoxicillin-clavulanate, or Ciprofloxacin 750 mg BD for Pseudomonas
investigations: sweat chloride/CFTR genetics in young patients.
precautions: Screen for NTM before long-term macrolide; ECG for QT; hearing monitoring.

name: Cystic Fibrosis
treatment: Multidisciplinary: airway clearance, CFTR modulators, nutrition, pancreatic enzyme replacement, infection control, transplant for end stage.
precautions: Cross-infection segregation (Burkholderia). CFTR modulators → monitor LFT, cataract checks in children, CYP3A drug interactions.

name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
treatment: Antifibrotics, pulmonary rehab, oxygen, vaccinations, treat GERD; lung transplant referral; palliative care.
medications: Nintedanib 150 mg BD or Pirfenidone 801 mg TDS (titrated)
investigations: autoimmune serology (ANA, RF, anti-CCP, myositis panel)
precautions: Nintedanib → diarrhea, LFT rise, bleeding risk. Pirfenidone → photosensitivity, take with food. Monitor LFTs monthly initially.

name: Sarcoidosis
treatment: Observation for asymptomatic stage I/II; treat if organ-threatening (cardiac, neuro, ocular, renal, hypercalcemia) or symptomatic pulmonary disease.
medications: Prednisolone 20–40 mg OD tapered over 6–12 months
precautions: Exclude TB before steroids in endemic regions. Bone protection on steroids.

name: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis
treatment: Antigen identification and avoidance (birds, molds, humidifiers); corticosteroids for symptomatic or fibrotic disease; antifibrotics for progressive fibrosis.
medications: Mycophenolate mofetil or Azathioprine as steroid-sparing
precautions: Complete antigen avoidance is essential; steroids alone do not halt disease if exposure continues.

name: Pneumothorax
treatment: Small primary, minimal symptoms → observation/outpatient; large or symptomatic → needle aspiration or small-bore chest drain; tension → immediate needle decompression (2nd ICS MCL or 4th/5th ICS AAL) then drain; recurrent → pleurodesis/VATS.
precautions: No air travel until resolved (1–2 weeks after resolution); no scuba diving lifelong unless definitive surgery. Smoking cessation.

name: Pleural Effusion
treatment: Treat cause; therapeutic thoracentesis if symptomatic; chest drain for empyema/complicated parapneumonic effusion; indwelling pleural catheter or pleurodesis for malignant effusion.
medications: Cause-specific: diuretics for heart failure, antibiotics for parapneumonic, ATT for tuberculous, intrapleural tPA + DNase for loculated empyema.
precautions: Remove ≤1.5 L at a time (re-expansion pulmonary edema). USG guidance reduces pneumothorax risk.

name: Empyema
treatment: Chest tube drainage + prolonged antibiotics (3–6 weeks); intrapleural fibrinolytics; VATS decortication if fails.
medications: intrapleural Alteplase 10 mg + Dornase 5 mg BD × 3 days (MIST-2).
precautions: Do not delay drainage; aminoglycosides penetrate pleura poorly.

name: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
treatment: Treat cause; lung-protective ventilation (tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight, plateau <30 cmH₂O), higher PEEP, prone positioning ≥16 h/day if P/F <150, conservative fluids; ECMO in refractory.
medications: Neuromuscular blockade (Cisatracurium) early in severe ARDS selectively
precautions: Avoid fluid overload; monitor for barotrauma; VAP prevention bundle.

name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
treatment: Weight loss, positional therapy, avoid alcohol/sedatives; CPAP for moderate–severe; mandibular advancement device; surgery or hypoglossal nerve stimulation in selected.
medications: Tirzepatide approved for moderate-severe OSA with obesity
Modafinil/Solriamfetol for residual sleepiness on CPAP.
investigations: polysomnography or home sleep apnea test (AHI ≥5 with symptoms, ≥15 regardless)
precautions: Drowsy-driving risk — counsel professional drivers. Avoid benzodiazepines/opioids. Pre-operative anesthetic alert.

name: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
treatment: Specialist centre; risk stratification; initial dual oral therapy for most; add parenteral prostacyclin for high risk; oxygen, diuretics, anticoagulation selected, transplant.
medications: Ambrisentan 5–10 mg OD or Macitentan 10 mg OD (ERA) + Tadalafil 40 mg OD or Sildenafil 20 mg TDS (PDE5i)
high-dose CCB only in vasoreactive patients.
differential_diagnoses: PH due to left heart disease
investigations: right heart catheterization (mPAP >20 mmHg, PVR >2 WU, PAWP ≤15)
precautions: ERAs teratogenic — contraception and pregnancy tests. No nitrates with PDE5i. Pregnancy contraindicated.

name: Lung Cancer (Non-Small Cell)
treatment: Staging-dependent: surgery (lobectomy) for early stage ± adjuvant/perioperative chemo-immunotherapy or Osimertinib (EGFR); chemoradiation + Durvalumab for stage III; targeted therapy or immunotherapy ± chemotherapy for stage IV based on biomarkers.
medications: ALK: Alectinib 600 mg BD or Lorlatinib
investigations: molecular testing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, HER2)
precautions: Immunotherapy → immune-related adverse events (pneumonitis, colitis, thyroiditis, hepatitis). Smoking cessation.

name: Small Cell Lung Cancer
treatment: Limited stage: concurrent chemoradiation ± consolidation Durvalumab, prophylactic cranial irradiation/MRI surveillance. Extensive stage: chemo-immunotherapy.
precautions: Watch tumour lysis, febrile neutropenia, paraneoplastic syndromes.

name: Silicosis / Pneumoconiosis
treatment: Remove from exposure; no specific therapy; treat complications (TB, COPD, respiratory failure); lung transplant; oxygen.
precautions: Workplace dust control, respirators, regular screening of workers (mining, stone cutting, sandblasting).

name: Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA)
treatment: Steroids to control inflammation, antifungals to reduce fungal burden; manage underlying asthma/CF.
medications: Prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg/day × 2–4 weeks then taper over 3–5 months
Itraconazole 200 mg BD × 16 weeks (alternative to steroids or adjunct)
precautions: Itraconazole interactions (CYP3A4) and hepatotoxicity; monitor IgE for relapse.

name: Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Aspergilloma
treatment: Asymptomatic simple aspergilloma → observation or surgery; chronic cavitary disease → long-term antifungal; hemoptysis → bronchial artery embolization or resection.
medications: Itraconazole 200 mg BD or Voriconazole 200 mg BD for ≥6 months
precautions: Therapeutic drug monitoring for azoles; voriconazole → visual disturbances, photosensitivity, skin cancer.

name: Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis
treatment: Urgent antifungal therapy in immunocompromised (neutropenia, transplant, high-dose steroids); reduce immunosuppression.
medications: Voriconazole 6 mg/kg IV q12h × 2 then 4 mg/kg q12h
Isavuconazole 200 mg q8h × 6 doses then OD
precautions: Voriconazole TDM (trough 1–5.5), many interactions (tacrolimus, cyclosporine). Amphotericin → nephrotoxicity, hypokalemia.

name: Pneumocystis Pneumonia (PJP)
treatment: Antimicrobial therapy 21 days; adjunct steroids if PaO₂ <70 mmHg (HIV); start ART within 2 weeks; secondary prophylaxis.
medications: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 15–20 mg/kg/day (TMP component) in 3–4 divided doses
Prednisone 40 mg BD × 5 days, 40 mg OD × 5 days, 20 mg OD × 11 days
alternatives: Primaquine + Clindamycin, Atovaquone. Prophylaxis: TMP-SMX 1 DS daily (CD4 <200).
precautions: TMP-SMX → hyperkalemia, rash/SJS, cytopenia. Check G6PD before primaquine/dapsone.

name: Acute Bronchitis
treatment: Supportive: fluids, rest, antipyretics; most are viral — antibiotics not indicated (except pertussis).
investigations: CXR if abnormal vitals or focal signs
precautions: Cough may last 3 weeks; avoid unnecessary antibiotics (resistance).

name: Influenza
treatment: Supportive care; antivirals within 48 h or anytime in high risk/hospitalized/severe disease; annual vaccination.
medications: Oseltamivir 75 mg BD × 5 days (adjust in renal impairment)
precautions: No aspirin in children (Reye syndrome). Watch secondary bacterial pneumonia (Staph aureus). Isolate.

name: COVID-19
treatment: Mild: symptomatic; high-risk mild: antivirals within 5 days; hospitalized hypoxic: oxygen, dexamethasone, anticoagulation prophylaxis, immunomodulators for progressive disease.
medications: Remdesivir 200 mg IV then 100 mg OD × 3–5 days
Dexamethasone 6 mg OD × 10 days (if requiring O₂)
Baricitinib or Tocilizumab for rapidly progressing
precautions: Ritonavir has major interactions (statins, anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, immunosuppressants) — check before prescribing. No steroids for non-hypoxic patients.

name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
treatment: Macrolide antibiotics (reduce transmission, shorten illness if early), supportive care, hospitalization for infants; prophylaxis for close contacts.
medications: Azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2–5 (children 10 mg/kg day 1 then 5 mg/kg)
precautions: Infants <6 months at risk of apnea; erythromycin in neonates → pyloric stenosis (prefer azithromycin). Tdap in pregnancy (27–36 weeks).

name: Diphtheria
treatment: Hospital isolation, diphtheria antitoxin urgently, antibiotics, airway protection; cardiac monitoring.
medications: Diphtheria antitoxin 20,000–100,000 units IV (after sensitivity test)
Penicillin G or Erythromycin 500 mg QID × 14 days
precautions: Notifiable disease; myocarditis and neuropathy may appear weeks later. Antitoxin anaphylaxis risk.

name: Hemoptysis (Massive)
treatment: Airway protection, position bleeding side down, intubation with large tube/selective, bronchoscopy, bronchial artery embolization, surgery.
medications: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV TDS or nebulized 500 mg
correct coagulopathy (vitamin K, FFP, reversal agents)
precautions: Death is from asphyxiation, not exsanguination — airway first.

name: Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Common Cold)
treatment: Self-limiting; symptomatic care, hydration, rest, hand hygiene.
medications: Zinc lozenges if started within 24 h.
precautions: Antibiotics not indicated. Avoid OTC cough/cold medicines in children <4–6 years. Decongestants → caution in hypertension. --- # 3. Gastrointestinal & Hepatobiliary

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
treatment: Weight loss, elevate head of bed, avoid late meals, reduce alcohol/caffeine/fatty foods, stop smoking; PPI 8 weeks then step down to lowest effective dose; anti-reflux surgery for refractory/regurgitation.
medications: Omeprazole 20–40 mg OD, Pantoprazole 40 mg OD, Esomeprazole 40 mg OD (30–60 min before breakfast)
investigations: endoscopy if alarm features (dysphagia, weight loss, bleeding, anemia, age >60 new onset)
precautions: Long-term PPI → B12/Mg deficiency, C. difficile, fracture risk — deprescribe when possible. Exclude cardiac cause of chest pain.

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
treatment: PPI, eradicate H. pylori, stop NSAIDs; endoscopic therapy if bleeding.
medications: Omeprazole 20–40 mg OD (BD with H. pylori) for 4–8 weeks
investigations: H. pylori testing (urea breath test, stool antigen, biopsy urease)
precautions: Stop PPI 2 weeks before H. pylori breath/stool test. Repeat endoscopy for gastric ulcers to confirm healing (exclude malignancy).

name: Helicobacter pylori Infection
treatment: Test-and-treat; confirm eradication ≥4 weeks after therapy. ACG 2024: optimized bismuth quadruple therapy 14 days first line; avoid empirical PPI-clarithromycin triple therapy unless clarithromycin susceptibility is confirmed.
medications: Bismuth quadruple: PPI BD + Bismuth subcitrate 120–300 mg or subsalicylate 262–524 mg QID + Tetracycline 500 mg QID + Metronidazole 500 mg TDS–QID × 14 days. Alternatives: Vonoprazan 20 mg BD + Amoxicillin 1 g TDS × 14 days
investigations: serology not for confirming active infection.
precautions: Metronidazole + alcohol → disulfiram-like reaction. Tetracycline contraindicated in pregnancy/children <8. Bismuth darkens stool/tongue.

name: Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding
treatment: Resuscitation (2 large-bore IV, restrictive transfusion Hb target 7–8 g/dL, 8 if cardiac disease), risk stratify (Glasgow-Blatchford), endoscopy within 24 h (within 12 h for variceal), endoscopic hemostasis; IR embolization or surgery if fails.
medications: Pantoprazole 80 mg IV bolus then 40 mg IV BD (or 8 mg/h) after endoscopic therapy for high-risk ulcers
Variceal: Terlipressin 2 mg IV q4h or Octreotide 50 mcg bolus then 50 mcg/h + Ceftriaxone 1 g OD prophylaxis
investigations: CT angiography if endoscopy negative and active bleeding.
precautions: Avoid tranexamic acid (HALT-IT — no benefit, more VTE). Manage anticoagulant reversal carefully.

name: Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding
treatment: Resuscitation, colonoscopy after bowel prep (within 24 h), endoscopic hemostasis; CT angiography + embolization if unstable; surgery rarely.
medications: reversal agents (Vitamin K, PCC, Idarucizumab, Andexanet).
precautions: Hematochezia with shock may be upper GI source — consider OGD first.

name: Functional Dyspepsia
treatment: Reassurance, test and treat H. pylori, PPI trial, then TCA or prokinetic; dietary modification; psychological therapy.
medications: Itopride 50 mg TDS or Domperidone 10 mg TDS (short term)
investigations: endoscopy if age >60 or alarm features.
precautions: Domperidone → QT prolongation (max 30 mg/day, short course). Metoclopramide → tardive dyskinesia (≤12 weeks).

name: Gastroparesis
treatment: Small frequent low-fat low-fibre meals, glycemic control, prokinetics, antiemetics; gastric electrical stimulation/G-POEM for refractory.
medications: Metoclopramide 5–10 mg TDS before meals (≤12 weeks)
precautions: Stop drugs that slow emptying (opioids, anticholinergics, GLP-1 RA) where possible.

name: Achalasia Cardia
treatment: Pneumatic dilation, laparoscopic Heller myotomy + fundoplication, or per-oral endoscopic myotomy (POEM); botulinum toxin for poor surgical candidates.
medications: Nifedipine 10–20 mg SL before meals or Isosorbide dinitrate 5 mg SL (limited efficacy)
precautions: Post-POEM reflux common — PPI surveillance. Increased risk of esophageal squamous cancer.

name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis
treatment: PPI, swallowed topical steroids, elimination diets, dilation for strictures, biologic for refractory.
medications: Budesonide orodispersible 1 mg BD or Fluticasone 880 mcg BD swallowed
precautions: Food bolus impaction is an emergency. Oral thrush with topical steroids.

name: Esophageal Cancer
treatment: Early: endoscopic resection. Locally advanced: neoadjuvant chemoradiation (CROSS) or perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT for adenocarcinoma) + esophagectomy; adjuvant Nivolumab if residual disease. Metastatic: chemotherapy ± immunotherapy; stenting for dysphagia.
precautions: Nutritional support (feeding jejunostomy); aspiration risk.

name: Gastric Cancer
treatment: Early: endoscopic submucosal dissection. Resectable: perioperative FLOT + gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy. Advanced: chemotherapy ± Nivolumab/Trastuzumab/Zolbetuximab (Claudin18.2).
precautions: Post-gastrectomy B12 and iron supplementation; dumping syndrome advice.

name: Acute Gastroenteritis
treatment: Oral rehydration (WHO low-osmolarity ORS), continue feeding, zinc in children; IV fluids if severe dehydration; antibiotics only for dysentery, cholera, severe traveler's diarrhea or immunocompromised.
medications: Ondansetron 4 mg (adults) single dose for vomiting
Loperamide 4 mg then 2 mg after each loose stool (max 16 mg/day) for non-bloody diarrhea in adults
Azithromycin 500 mg OD × 3 days for invasive diarrhea.
precautions: No loperamide for bloody diarrhea or children <2. Avoid antibiotics in suspected STEC/EHEC (HUS risk). Hand hygiene.

name: Cholera
treatment: Aggressive rehydration is life-saving (ORS; IV Ringer's lactate if severe — 100 mL/kg over 3 h adults); single-dose antibiotics in moderate–severe cases; zinc in children.
medications: Azithromycin 1 g single dose (children 20 mg/kg, pregnant women)
Ciprofloxacin 1 g single dose where susceptible.
precautions: Watch hypokalemia, hypoglycemia (children). Notifiable. Safe water, oral cholera vaccine in outbreaks.

name: Amoebic Dysentery & Amoebic Liver Abscess
treatment: Tissue amoebicide followed by luminal agent; aspiration of liver abscess if large (>5 cm), left lobe or no response in 72 h.
medications: Metronidazole 750 mg TDS × 7–10 days (or Tinidazole 2 g OD × 3–5 days), then Paromomycin 25–35 mg/kg/day in 3 doses × 7 days or Diloxanide furoate 500 mg TDS × 10 days.
precautions: No alcohol with metronidazole/tinidazole. Avoid antimotility agents. Watch rupture of left-lobe abscess into pericardium.

name: Bacillary Dysentery (Shigellosis)
treatment: Hydration, antibiotics for moderate–severe disease.
medications: Ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV OD × 3–5 days for severe.
precautions: Rising fluoroquinolone resistance in South Asia. Avoid antimotility drugs.

name: Clostridioides difficile Infection
treatment: Stop inciting antibiotic, contact precautions, oral antibiotics; fecal microbiota transplant for multiple recurrences; colectomy for fulminant colitis.
medications: Fidaxomicin 200 mg BD × 10 days (preferred) or Vancomycin 125 mg PO QID × 10 days
Fulminant: Vancomycin 500 mg PO/NG QID + Metronidazole 500 mg IV TDS ± rectal vancomycin
investigations: Stool GDH + toxin EIA ± PCR (only unformed stools)
precautions: Alcohol hand rub does not kill spores — use soap and water. Avoid antimotility agents. Avoid unnecessary PPIs.

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
treatment: Education, diet (low FODMAP under dietitian, soluble fibre), exercise, CBT/gut-directed hypnotherapy, symptom-targeted drugs.
medications: IBS-C: Psyllium, Polyethylene glycol, Linaclotide 290 mcg OD, Lubiprostone. IBS-D: Loperamide, Rifaximin 550 mg TDS × 14 days, Eluxadoline, Ondansetron. Pain: Mebeverine 135 mg TDS, Peppermint oil, Hyoscine butylbromide, Amitriptyline 10–30 mg at night.
precautions: Alarm features (rectal bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms, family history of CRC, anemia) need investigation.

name: Ulcerative Colitis
treatment: Induce and maintain remission by extent and severity; acute severe UC → hospital, IV steroids, rescue therapy by day 3; colectomy for refractory/dysplasia.
medications: Infliximab, Vedolizumab, Ustekinumab, Mirikizumab, Tofacitinib, Upadacitinib, Ozanimod, Etrasimod
precautions: VTE prophylaxis in hospitalized patients. Colonoscopic dysplasia surveillance 8 years after onset. Avoid NSAIDs and antimotility drugs in flares. JAK inhibitors → VTE/MACE warnings.

name: Crohn's Disease
treatment: Steroid induction or early advanced therapy for moderate–severe; maintenance with biologics/immunomodulators; surgery for strictures/fistulae/abscess; nutritional therapy; stop smoking.
medications: Infliximab 5 mg/kg (weeks 0, 2, 6 then q8w) or Adalimumab 160/80 then 40 mg q2w
precautions: Rule out intestinal TB before steroids/biologics. Smoking worsens Crohn's. Live vaccines contraindicated on biologics.

name: Celiac Disease
treatment: Lifelong strict gluten-free diet (wheat, barley, rye); dietitian; correct deficiencies; vaccinate (pneumococcal — hyposplenism).
medications: Iron, folate, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D and calcium supplements as needed
precautions: Do not start gluten-free diet before testing. Higher risk of lymphoma (EATL) if non-adherent.

name: Acute Appendicitis
treatment: Laparoscopic appendectomy; antibiotics-first approach for selected uncomplicated cases (CT-confirmed, no appendicolith); percutaneous drainage + interval surgery for abscess.
medications: Pre-op Cefazolin 2 g + Metronidazole 500 mg IV
non-operative: Ertapenem 1 g IV then oral Amoxicillin-clavulanate or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole for total 7–10 days
precautions: Always do a pregnancy test in women of reproductive age. Perforation risk rises after 36–48 h.

name: Acute Pancreatitis
treatment: Early goal-directed moderate fluid resuscitation (Ringer's lactate, avoid aggressive overload), analgesia, early oral/enteral feeding; ERCP within 24–72 h only if cholangitis; cholecystectomy same admission for mild gallstone pancreatitis; step-up approach for infected necrosis.
medications: Ringer's lactate 1.5 mL/kg/h after 10 mL/kg bolus if hypovolemic
investigations: CT with contrast after 72 h if diagnosis unclear/deterioration
precautions: No prophylactic antibiotics. Alcohol abstinence. Monitor for organ failure, ARDS, hypocalcemia.

name: Chronic Pancreatitis
treatment: Abstinence from alcohol and smoking, pain management, pancreatic enzyme replacement, diabetes management; endoscopic or surgical decompression for ductal stones/strictures.
medications: Pancrelipase 40,000–50,000 lipase units with meals, 25,000 with snacks
precautions: Increased pancreatic cancer risk; screen for osteoporosis. Avoid opioid dependence.

name: Pancreatic Cancer
treatment: Resectable: surgery (Whipple) + adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX. Borderline: neoadjuvant therapy. Metastatic: FOLFIRINOX/NALIRIFOX or Gemcitabine + nab-Paclitaxel; biliary stenting, celiac plexus block for pain.
precautions: New-onset diabetes with weight loss in >50 years — consider pancreatic cancer. VTE risk high.

name: Acute Cholecystitis
treatment: NPO, IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics; early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 72 h–7 days); percutaneous cholecystostomy if high surgical risk.
medications: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD + Metronidazole 500 mg IV TDS, or Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q8h (severe)
investigations: USG (thick wall, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy)
precautions: Watch gangrene/perforation in diabetics and elderly. Tokyo Guidelines 2018 severity.

name: Cholelithiasis (Gallstones) / Biliary Colic
treatment: Asymptomatic → no treatment usually. Symptomatic → elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Low-fat diet.
medications: Diclofenac 75 mg IM or Ketorolac for colic
Ursodeoxycholic acid 10–15 mg/kg/day for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical candidates/after bariatric surgery.
precautions: Porcelain gallbladder or polyp >10 mm → cholecystectomy (cancer risk).

name: Acute Cholangitis / Choledocholithiasis
treatment: Antibiotics, fluids, biliary drainage by ERCP (urgent within 24 h if severe), then cholecystectomy.
medications: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h or Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole
precautions: Charcot triad/Reynolds pentad → emergency. Correct coagulopathy before ERCP.

name: Acute Viral Hepatitis A
treatment: Supportive; rest, hydration, avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs; hospitalize if INR elevated/encephalopathy.
medications: post-exposure Hepatitis A vaccine within 2 weeks.
precautions: Fecal–oral spread; food handlers excluded until 1 week after jaundice onset. Watch for acute liver failure.

name: Hepatitis E
treatment: Supportive; ribavirin for chronic HEV in immunosuppressed.
precautions: High mortality (up to 20–25%) in pregnant women (third trimester) — close monitoring. Ribavirin teratogenic.

name: Chronic Hepatitis B
treatment: Antivirals per HBV DNA, ALT, fibrosis (WHO 2024 expanded eligibility); HCC surveillance; vaccinate contacts.
medications: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg OD, Tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg OD or Entecavir 0.5 mg OD (1 mg if lamivudine-exposed)
precautions: Do not stop antivirals abruptly (flare). Prophylaxis before chemotherapy/rituximab. TDF → renal/bone; prefer TAF in CKD/osteoporosis. TDF in third trimester if high viral load to prevent transmission.

name: Chronic Hepatitis C
treatment: Pan-genotypic direct-acting antivirals (cure >95%); assess fibrosis; HCC surveillance if cirrhotic.
precautions: Screen HBsAg before DAA (HBV reactivation). Sofosbuvir + amiodarone → severe bradycardia. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis.

name: Alcohol-Related Hepatitis
treatment: Abstinence, nutrition (35–40 kcal/kg, 1.2–1.5 g/kg protein), thiamine, treat withdrawal and infection; steroids if Maddrey ≥32/MELD >20; early transplant in selected.
medications: Prednisolone 40 mg OD × 28 days (stop if Lille score >0.45 at day 7)
precautions: Exclude infection and GI bleed before steroids. Avoid disulfiram and naltrexone in severe liver disease.

name: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD/NAFLD)
treatment: Weight loss 7–10% (diet + exercise), manage diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension; avoid alcohol; MASH with fibrosis → pharmacotherapy; bariatric surgery for obesity.
medications: statins safe and indicated for CV risk.
precautions: Cardiovascular disease is the main cause of death — address risk factors. Vitamin E long-term → possible prostate cancer/hemorrhagic stroke risk.

name: Liver Cirrhosis
treatment: Treat cause, abstinence, nutrition (late-evening snack), vaccination, varices screening, HCC surveillance, manage decompensation; transplant referral (MELD ≥15).
investigations: etiology screen (HBV, HCV, ferritin, ceruloplasmin, autoimmune).
precautions: Avoid NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, sedatives (benzodiazepines). Paracetamol ≤2 g/day. Avoid ACEi/ARB in ascites.

name: Ascites (Cirrhotic) & Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis
treatment: Sodium restriction (<2 g/day = 5 g salt), diuretics, large-volume paracentesis with albumin, TIPS for refractory; SBP → antibiotics + albumin.
medications: Albumin 6–8 g per litre removed (>5 L paracentesis)
SBP: Cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h or Ceftriaxone 1–2 g OD × 5 days + Albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1, 1 g/kg day 3
precautions: Stop diuretics if Na <125, creatinine rising, encephalopathy. Monitor for hepatorenal syndrome.

name: Hepatic Encephalopathy
treatment: Identify and correct precipitants (infection, GI bleed, constipation, hypokalemia, sedatives, dehydration); lactulose; rifaximin for recurrence prevention; nutrition (don't restrict protein).
medications: Lactulose 25 mL every 1–2 h until bowel movement then titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day
precautions: Avoid benzodiazepines/opioids. Protect airway in grade 3–4.

name: Esophageal Varices
treatment: Primary prophylaxis (non-selective beta-blocker or endoscopic band ligation); acute bleed → vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, EBL within 12 h, TIPS (pre-emptive in Child C); secondary prophylaxis NSBB + EBL.
precautions: Avoid over-transfusion (raises portal pressure). Hold NSBB if refractory ascites with SBP ≤90 or AKI.

name: Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI)
treatment: Stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, volume expansion with albumin, vasoconstrictor therapy; liver transplantation definitive.
medications: Albumin 1 g/kg (max 100 g) for 2 days, then 20–40 g/day
Terlipressin 1 mg IV q4–6h (or 2 mg/day infusion) up to 12 mg/day
precautions: Terlipressin → ischemia, pulmonary edema/respiratory failure — avoid if SpO₂ <90%; monitor fluid status.

name: Acute Liver Failure
treatment: ICU at transplant centre; identify cause (paracetamol, viral, DILI); NAC; manage cerebral edema, coagulopathy, infection, hypoglycemia; urgent transplant evaluation (King's College criteria).
medications: N-acetylcysteine IV 150 mg/kg over 1 h, 50 mg/kg over 4 h, 100 mg/kg over 16 h (also benefits non-paracetamol ALF in early stage)
precautions: Avoid sedatives; don't correct INR routinely (prognostic marker) unless bleeding/procedure.

name: Autoimmune Hepatitis
treatment: Immunosuppression to induce remission (normal ALT and IgG), maintenance ≥2–3 years; transplant for liver failure.
medications: Prednisolone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day tapered or Budesonide 9 mg/day (non-cirrhotic) + Azathioprine 1–2 mg/kg/day
precautions: Bone protection; TPMT testing before azathioprine. Budesonide ineffective in cirrhosis (portosystemic shunting).

name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis
treatment: Lifelong ursodeoxycholic acid; second-line for inadequate response; manage pruritus, osteoporosis, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency; transplant.
medications: Elafibranor 80 mg OD or Seladelpar 10 mg OD (second line)
Cholestyramine 4 g (4 h apart from UDCA) or Bezafibrate for pruritus.
precautions: Monitor ALP response at 12 months. Screen for thyroid disease, Sjögren's.

name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
treatment: No proven medical therapy; ERCP dilation of dominant strictures; manage cholangitis; surveillance for cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, colorectal cancer (with IBD); transplant.
precautions: Annual colonoscopy if associated UC. High-dose UDCA harmful.

name: Wilson Disease
treatment: Lifelong copper chelation or zinc; low-copper diet (avoid shellfish, liver, nuts, chocolate initially); liver transplant for fulminant disease.
medications: D-Penicillamine 750–1500 mg/day in divided doses + Pyridoxine 25 mg
precautions: Penicillamine may worsen neurological symptoms initially; side effects (nephrotic syndrome, cytopenias, lupus-like). Screen siblings.

name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis
treatment: Therapeutic phlebotomy (500 mL weekly) until ferritin 50–100 µg/L, then maintenance; chelation if phlebotomy not tolerated.
precautions: Avoid iron and vitamin C supplements, raw shellfish (Vibrio vulnificus). HCC surveillance if cirrhosis.

name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
treatment: BCLC staging: resection, transplantation (Milan criteria), ablation for early; TACE intermediate; systemic therapy advanced.
precautions: Screen varices before bevacizumab (bleeding risk). Treat HBV with antivirals concurrently.

name: Colorectal Cancer
treatment: Colon: surgery ± adjuvant chemotherapy (stage III, high-risk II). Rectal: total neoadjuvant therapy + TME surgery or watch-and-wait. dMMR/MSI-H: immunotherapy (Dostarlimab for dMMR rectal). Metastatic: chemotherapy + biologics.
precautions: Screening from age 45 (FIT yearly or colonoscopy every 10 years). Oxaliplatin → neuropathy; Capecitabine → hand-foot syndrome; DPD deficiency testing before fluoropyrimidines.

name: Diverticulitis
treatment: Uncomplicated: outpatient, clear liquids, selective antibiotics; complicated: IV antibiotics, percutaneous drainage of abscess >3–4 cm, surgery for perforation/peritonitis.
medications: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BD or Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD + Metronidazole 500 mg TDS × 4–7 days
IV Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole or Piperacillin-tazobactam for complicated.
investigations: colonoscopy 6–8 weeks after if not recently done.
precautions: High-fibre diet for prevention; nuts and seeds need not be avoided. Avoid NSAIDs/opioids long-term.

name: Hemorrhoids
treatment: Fibre 25–35 g/day, fluids, avoid straining; office procedures (rubber band ligation) for grade I–III; hemorrhoidectomy for grade III–IV or thrombosed external (<72 h).
precautions: Do not attribute rectal bleeding to hemorrhoids without excluding malignancy in at-risk patients. Prolonged steroid creams → skin atrophy.

name: Anal Fissure
treatment: Fibre, sitz baths, topical agents for 6–8 weeks; botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy for chronic fissure.
medications: Diltiazem 2% ointment BD or Glyceryl trinitrate 0.2–0.4% ointment BD
precautions: GTN causes headaches. Sphincterotomy → small risk of incontinence.

name: Perianal Abscess & Fistula-in-Ano
treatment: Abscess: prompt incision and drainage. Fistula: fistulotomy (low), seton, LIFT, advancement flap for complex fistulae.
medications: Antibiotics only if cellulitis, immunocompromised, diabetes or systemic sepsis: Amoxicillin-clavulanate or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole
precautions: Antibiotics alone do not treat abscess. Screen for Crohn's disease and diabetes in recurrent cases. --- # 4. Renal & Urology

name: Acute Kidney Injury
treatment: Identify cause (pre-renal, intrinsic, post-renal); restore volume, stop nephrotoxins, relieve obstruction, treat complications; dialysis for refractory hyperkalemia, acidosis, overload, uremia, toxins (AEIOU).
investigations: autoimmune screen (ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, complements) if GN suspected.
precautions: Stop/adjust ACEi, ARB, NSAIDs, metformin, aminoglycosides, SGLT2i ("sick day rules"). Renally dose all drugs.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
treatment: Slow progression (BP <120–130 systolic per KDIGO, RAAS blockade, SGLT2i), manage complications (anemia, mineral-bone disease, acidosis, hyperkalemia), CV risk reduction, prepare for renal replacement therapy (eGFR <15).
medications: Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD or Empagliflozin 10 mg OD (eGFR ≥20)
Finerenone 10–20 mg OD (diabetic CKD with albuminuria)
Sodium bicarbonate 500–1000 mg BD–TDS if HCO₃ <22
precautions: Avoid NSAIDs, nephrotoxins, gadolinium (eGFR <30), metformin <30. Dose-adjust drugs. Hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis. Preserve forearm veins for AV fistula.

name: End-Stage Kidney Disease (Dialysis)
treatment: Hemodialysis (AV fistula preferred) or peritoneal dialysis; kidney transplantation is best option; conservative kidney management in frail elderly.
medications: ESA (Epoetin alfa 50–100 IU/kg 3×/week), IV iron sucrose, phosphate binders, Calcitriol/Paricalcitol, Cinacalcet, Vitamin B complex, antihypertensives
precautions: Restrict fluids, potassium (bananas, coconut water), phosphate. Never use the AV fistula arm for BP/cannula.

name: Nephrotic Syndrome (Adult)
treatment: Treat cause (biopsy-guided), RAAS blockade, diuretics, salt restriction, statin, anticoagulation if high thrombotic risk (albumin <2.0–2.5 g/dL in membranous).
precautions: Risk of thrombosis (renal vein), infections, AKI with over-diuresis. Prophylaxis on steroids (PJP, bone).

name: Childhood Nephrotic Syndrome (Minimal Change Disease)
treatment: Corticosteroids (most are steroid-sensitive), salt restriction, manage edema; steroid-sparing agents for frequent relapses.
medications: Prednisolone 60 mg/m²/day (max 60 mg) × 6 weeks, then 40 mg/m² alternate days × 6 weeks
Levamisole, Cyclophosphamide, MMF, Tacrolimus, Rituximab for frequently relapsing/steroid-dependent
precautions: Risk of peritonitis (pneumococcal), thrombosis. Avoid live vaccines on high-dose steroids. Daily urine dipstick monitoring for relapse.

name: IgA Nephropathy
treatment: Optimized supportive care (RAAS blockade to max dose, BP <120–125 systolic, SGLT2i); targeted therapies if proteinuria persists >0.5–1 g/day.
precautions: Sparsentan → hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity monitoring. Systemic steroids → infections (TESTING trial).

name: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis
treatment: Supportive: salt and fluid restriction, diuretics, antihypertensives; antibiotics to eradicate strep; dialysis rarely.
precautions: Persistent low C3 >8 weeks suggests C3 glomerulopathy/MPGN — biopsy.

name: Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis / ANCA Vasculitis Renal
treatment: Emergency nephrology; high-dose steroids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange for anti-GBM disease; dialysis as needed.
medications: Methylprednisolone 500–1000 mg IV × 3 days then oral Prednisolone (reduced-dose PEXIVAS regimen)
precautions: PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX), infection risk, bone protection. Don't delay treatment awaiting biopsy if critically ill.

name: Lupus Nephritis
treatment: Induction then maintenance immunosuppression by ISN/RPS class; hydroxychloroquine for all; RAAS blockade; BP and lipid control.
medications: Mycophenolate mofetil 2–3 g/day or Euro-Lupus IV Cyclophosphamide 500 mg q2w × 6 + steroids
precautions: MMF teratogenic — contraception. Hydroxychloroquine → annual eye screening after 5 years.

name: Diabetic Kidney Disease
treatment: Glycemic control, BP control, four-pillar kidney protection (RAAS blockade, SGLT2i, non-steroidal MRA, GLP-1 RA), statin, smoking cessation.
medications: Losartan/Telmisartan or Ramipril at max tolerated dose
differential_diagnoses: non-diabetic GN (if rapid decline, hematuria, no retinopathy)
precautions: Monitor K⁺ with ACEi/ARB + finerenone. Adjust insulin/sulfonylureas (hypoglycemia) as GFR falls.

name: Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
treatment: BP control (ACEi/ARB, target ≤110/75 in young), high water intake, low salt, treat pain/infections; vasopressin antagonist for rapidly progressive disease; RRT.
medications: Tolvaptan 45/15 mg titrated to 90/30 mg daily (split doses).
investigations: MR angiography for intracranial aneurysm if family history.
precautions: Tolvaptan → hepatotoxicity (monthly LFT × 18 months), polyuria. Avoid NSAIDs; avoid contact sports with large kidneys.

name: Urinary Tract Infection — Uncomplicated Cystitis
treatment: Short-course antibiotics, hydration; self-limiting in some.
precautions: Avoid nitrofurantoin if eGFR <30 and at term pregnancy. Avoid fluoroquinolones for simple cystitis (adverse effects). Don't treat asymptomatic bacteriuria except in pregnancy/before urological procedures.

name: Acute Pyelonephritis
treatment: Antibiotics 7–14 days; IV therapy if vomiting/septic; imaging if not improving in 48–72 h (abscess, obstruction).
medications: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD × 7 days or Levofloxacin 750 mg OD × 5 days (if local resistance <10%)
precautions: In pregnancy use ceftriaxone (avoid fluoroquinolones). Obstructed infected kidney is a urological emergency (decompress).

name: Recurrent UTI in Women
treatment: Behavioral measures (hydration, post-coital voiding), vaginal estrogen in post-menopausal women, non-antibiotic and antibiotic prophylaxis.
precautions: Long-term nitrofurantoin → pulmonary/hepatic toxicity — monitor.

name: Urolithiasis (Kidney Stones) / Renal Colic
treatment: Analgesia, hydration; medical expulsive therapy for distal ureteric stones 5–10 mm; ureteroscopy, ESWL, PCNL for large/obstructing stones; urgent decompression if infected obstruction.
medications: Diclofenac 75 mg IM/IV or Ketorolac 30 mg IV (first line)
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg OD × up to 4 weeks
investigations: 24-h urine metabolic profile in recurrent formers.
precautions: Fever + obstruction = emergency. Fluid intake for >2.5 L urine/day; reduce salt and animal protein; don't restrict dietary calcium.

name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
treatment: Watchful waiting for mild symptoms; alpha-blockers; 5-ARI for prostate >30–40 mL; combination; surgery (TURP, HoLEP, Rezum, UroLift) for refractory, retention, recurrent UTI, stones, renal impairment.
medications: Tamsulosin 0.4 mg OD, Silodosin 8 mg OD, Alfuzosin 10 mg OD
Finasteride 5 mg OD or Dutasteride 0.5 mg OD
precautions: Alpha-blockers → orthostatic hypotension, floppy iris syndrome (inform before cataract surgery). 5-ARIs halve PSA. Avoid anticholinergics/decongestants if retention risk.

name: Acute Urinary Retention
treatment: Immediate urethral catheterization (suprapubic if urethral fails); start alpha-blocker and trial without catheter after 2–3 days; treat cause.
precautions: Watch post-obstructive diuresis and hematuria after decompression.

name: Acute Bacterial Prostatitis
treatment: Antibiotics 2–4 weeks; hospitalize if septic or retention (suprapubic catheter preferred).
medications: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD or Levofloxacin 500 mg OD × 2–4 weeks
precautions: Avoid vigorous prostatic massage (bacteremia). PSA rises transiently — do not test during infection.

name: Chronic Prostatitis / Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome
treatment: Multimodal (UPOINT): alpha-blockers, analgesics, pelvic floor physiotherapy, psychological support; antibiotics only if bacterial.
precautions: Avoid repeated empirical antibiotic courses.

name: Prostate Cancer
treatment: Low risk: active surveillance. Localized intermediate/high: radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy + ADT. Metastatic: ADT + androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor ± docetaxel; PARP inhibitors, Lu-177-PSMA for mCRPC.
differential_diagnoses: other causes of raised PSA (recent catheterization, ejaculation, UTI).
precautions: ADT → osteoporosis, metabolic syndrome, CV risk — bone protection (Denosumab/Zoledronic acid). Flare with GnRH agonist — give antiandrogen first.

name: Bladder Cancer
treatment: Non-muscle invasive: TURBT + intravesical BCG/chemotherapy. Muscle-invasive: neoadjuvant cisplatin chemo + radical cystectomy or trimodality therapy. Metastatic: Enfortumab vedotin + Pembrolizumab.
precautions: Painless visible hematuria in adults = urgent cystoscopy. Smoking is main risk factor.

name: Renal Cell Carcinoma
treatment: Localized: partial or radical nephrectomy; ablation for small masses; adjuvant Pembrolizumab for high risk. Metastatic: immunotherapy combinations.
precautions: Monitor immune-related adverse events; TKI → hypertension, hand-foot syndrome, hypothyroidism.

name: Testicular Torsion
treatment: Surgical emergency — scrotal exploration, detorsion and bilateral orchidopexy within 6 h; orchiectomy if non-viable. Manual detorsion ("open the book") as temporizing measure.
medications: no medical treatment substitutes for surgery.
investigations: Clinical diagnosis (high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex)
Doppler USG if diagnosis uncertain — do not delay surgery.
precautions: Time-critical: salvage >90% if <6 h, <10% after 24 h.

name: Epididymo-orchitis
treatment: Antibiotics based on age/risk (STI vs enteric), scrotal support, analgesia; partner treatment if STI.
medications: STI risk (<35 years): Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose + Doxycycline 100 mg BD × 10 days
enteric risk: Levofloxacin 500 mg OD × 10 days or Ofloxacin.
precautions: Always exclude torsion in adolescents. Screen for other STIs including HIV and syphilis.

name: Erectile Dysfunction
treatment: Address CV risk factors, lifestyle, psychological factors; PDE5 inhibitors first line; vacuum devices, intracavernosal injections, penile prosthesis.
medications: Tadalafil 10–20 mg PRN or 5 mg OD
precautions: PDE5i contraindicated with nitrates/riociguat; caution with alpha-blockers. Priapism >4 h = emergency. ED may be first sign of CAD.

name: Overactive Bladder
treatment: Bladder training, fluid/caffeine management, pelvic floor exercises; antimuscarinics or beta-3 agonist; botulinum toxin, sacral/tibial neuromodulation.
medications: Mirabegron 25–50 mg OD or Vibegron 75 mg OD
Solifenacin 5–10 mg OD, Tolterodine 2 mg BD, Trospium 20 mg BD (less CNS penetration)
precautions: Antimuscarinics → cognitive impairment in elderly (anticholinergic burden), constipation, dry mouth, retention. Mirabegron → monitor BP.

name: Stress Urinary Incontinence
treatment: Pelvic floor muscle training ≥3 months, weight loss; vaginal pessary; surgery (mid-urethral sling, colposuspension, bulking agents).
precautions: Duloxetine → nausea, suicidal ideation monitoring.

name: Hyperkalemia
treatment: ECG changes or K⁺ ≥6.5 = emergency: stabilize myocardium, shift K⁺ into cells, remove K⁺; dialysis if refractory/renal failure.
medications: Calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV over 5–10 min (repeat if ECG changes persist)
Insulin regular 10 U IV + Dextrose 25 g (monitor glucose)
Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g TDS or Patiromer 8.4 g OD
investigations: ECG (peaked T, wide QRS, sine wave)
precautions: Calcium does not lower K⁺ — it's membrane protection. Rebound after insulin/salbutamol wears off — recheck.

name: Hyponatremia
treatment: Severe symptomatic (seizures, coma): 3% hypertonic saline 100–150 mL bolus over 10–20 min, repeat up to 3 times; target rise 4–6 mmol/L. Chronic: treat cause — fluid restriction (SIADH), isotonic saline (hypovolemic), diuretics (hypervolemic).
precautions: Limit correction to ≤8–10 mmol/L in 24 h (osmotic demyelination). High-risk (alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia): ≤8 mmol/L. Stop thiazides.

name: Hypokalemia
treatment: Replace potassium (oral preferred); IV if K⁺ <2.5, ECG changes, or unable to take orally; correct magnesium; treat cause.
medications: IV KCl 10 mmol/h peripheral (max 20 mmol/h central with monitoring)
precautions: Never give IV potassium as bolus. Hypokalemia worsens digoxin toxicity and arrhythmias. --- # 5. Endocrine & Metabolic

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
treatment: Lifestyle (medical nutrition therapy, 150 min/week activity, 5–15% weight loss); individualized HbA1c target (generally <7%); choose agents by comorbidity (ADA 2025/2026 Standards): SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA for ASCVD, HF, CKD; metformin foundation; insulin if very high glucose or catabolic.
medications: Metformin 500 mg OD → 1000 mg BD (XR available)
Semaglutide 0.25→1–2 mg SC weekly or oral 3→14 mg
Basal insulin Glargine 10 U or 0.1–0.2 U/kg at bedtime, titrate.
precautions: Metformin: stop if eGFR <30, hold for iodinated contrast in AKI risk; lactic acidosis rare. Sulfonylureas/insulin → hypoglycemia. SGLT2i → euglycemic DKA, genital mycotic infections (sick-day rules). GLP-1 RA → pancreatitis, contraindicated with MTC/MEN2 history.

name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
treatment: Lifelong insulin (basal-bolus or pump), carbohydrate counting, CGM, structured education, screening for complications and autoimmune diseases; Teplizumab to delay onset in stage 2.
medications: Insulin glargine/degludec/detemir (basal ~50% of total daily dose 0.4–1 U/kg/day) + rapid-acting aspart/lispro/glulisine with meals
Glucagon (nasal 3 mg or IM 1 mg) for severe hypoglycemia.
precautions: Never stop basal insulin, even if not eating (sick-day rules — check ketones). Hypoglycemia awareness; driving rules (check glucose >90 mg/dL before driving).

name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
treatment: Fluids, IV insulin, potassium replacement, treat precipitant (infection, missed insulin, MI); resolution: glucose <200 + 2 of (HCO₃ ≥15, pH >7.3, anion gap ≤12).
medications: 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 1–1.5 L first hour
Regular insulin 0.1 U/kg/h fixed-rate infusion (only if K⁺ ≥3.5)
Potassium chloride 20–40 mmol/L of fluid if K⁺ <5.0
overlap SC basal insulin 1–2 h before stopping infusion.
precautions: Hypokalemia is the main killer — check K⁺ before insulin. Cerebral edema in children — avoid rapid fluid shifts. Check for SGLT2i euglycemic DKA.

name: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State
treatment: Careful fluid replacement (major deficit 8–12 L), low-dose insulin after fluids lower glucose, potassium, treat cause, VTE prophylaxis.
medications: 0.9% saline 1 L/h initially then guided by osmolality
Insulin 0.05 U/kg/h once glucose stops falling with fluids alone (or with ketonemia)
precautions: Correct osmolality slowly (≤3–8 mOsm/kg/h) and sodium ≤10 mmol/L/24 h. High thrombosis risk.

name: Hypoglycemia
treatment: Conscious: 15–20 g fast-acting glucose, recheck in 15 min, repeat; then complex carbohydrate. Unconscious: IV dextrose or glucagon. Identify cause.
medications: Glucagon 1 mg IM/SC or 3 mg nasal
Octreotide 50 mcg SC for sulfonylurea overdose.
precautions: Sulfonylurea hypoglycemia can recur — observe 24 h. Glucagon ineffective in depleted glycogen (alcohol, starvation).

name: Prediabetes & Metabolic Syndrome
treatment: Intensive lifestyle (7% weight loss, 150 min/week activity — DPP trial: 58% risk reduction); treat BP/lipids; metformin in high-risk.
medications: Metformin 500–850 mg BD (BMI ≥35, age <60, prior GDM)
precautions: Annual glucose testing. Asian Indian cut-off for waist: ≥90 cm men, ≥80 cm women.

name: Obesity
treatment: Comprehensive lifestyle (calorie deficit 500–750 kcal/day, activity, behavior therapy); pharmacotherapy for BMI ≥30 (≥27 with comorbidity; Asian thresholds lower ≥25/23); metabolic/bariatric surgery for BMI ≥35 (≥27.5 Asian with T2DM).
precautions: GLP-1/GIP agonists → GI effects, gallstones, pancreatitis, muscle loss (ensure protein/resistance training); contraindicated in pregnancy and MEN2/MTC history.

name: Hypothyroidism (Primary)
treatment: Levothyroxine replacement, titrate to TSH in reference range; subclinical (TSH 4.5–10) treat selectively (symptoms, pregnancy, antibodies, TSH >10).
medications: Levothyroxine 1.6 mcg/kg/day (start 25–50 mcg in elderly/cardiac disease) on empty stomach 30–60 min before breakfast
investigations: repeat TSH 6–8 weeks after dose change.
precautions: Separate from iron, calcium, PPIs (4 h). Over-replacement → AF, osteoporosis. Rule out adrenal insufficiency before thyroxine in panhypopituitarism.

name: Myxedema Coma
treatment: ICU; IV thyroid hormone, steroids until adrenal insufficiency excluded, supportive ventilation, passive rewarming, treat hyponatremia/hypoglycemia and precipitant.
medications: Levothyroxine 200–400 mcg IV loading then 50–100 mcg IV daily (± Liothyronine 5–20 mcg IV)
precautions: Lower doses in elderly/coronary disease (ischemia risk). Avoid sedatives.

name: Graves' Disease / Hyperthyroidism
treatment: Antithyroid drugs 12–18 months, radioactive iodine, or thyroidectomy; beta-blockers for symptoms; smoking cessation (eye disease).
medications: Carbimazole 20–40 mg/day or Methimazole 10–30 mg OD (titrate/block-replace)
Propylthiouracil 50–150 mg TDS in first trimester/thyroid storm
Teprotumumab for moderate-severe thyroid eye disease
precautions: Agranulocytosis (sore throat + fever → stop and check CBC). PTU → hepatotoxicity (avoid except 1st trimester/storm). Methimazole teratogenic early pregnancy. Radioiodine contraindicated in pregnancy/breastfeeding; may worsen eye disease (steroid cover).

name: Thyroid Storm
treatment: ICU; block synthesis, block release, beta-blockade, steroids, treat precipitant, supportive (cooling, fluids).
medications: PTU 500–1000 mg load then 250 mg q4h (or Methimazole 20 mg q4–6h)
1 h later Lugol's iodine 8–10 drops q6–8h or SSKI 5 drops q6h
Hydrocortisone 300 mg IV load then 100 mg q8h
precautions: Give thionamide before iodine (avoid fuelling hormone synthesis). Avoid aspirin (displaces T4 from binding proteins).

name: Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis
treatment: Anti-inflammatory therapy, beta-blockers for thyrotoxic phase; temporary levothyroxine for hypothyroid phase if symptomatic.
medications: Prednisolone 40 mg/day tapered over 4–6 weeks if severe
precautions: Antithyroid drugs are ineffective (no excess synthesis).

name: Thyroid Nodule & Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
treatment: Benign nodules — surveillance. Papillary/follicular cancer — lobectomy or total thyroidectomy ± radioactive iodine; TSH suppression as per risk; active surveillance for low-risk microcarcinoma.
precautions: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia and recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Low-iodine diet before RAI.

name: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
treatment: Parathyroidectomy if symptomatic or meets criteria (Ca >1 mg/dL above ULN, osteoporosis/vertebral fracture, eGFR <60, kidney stones/hypercalciuria, age <50); medical therapy otherwise.
precautions: Avoid thiazides, dehydration, lithium. Maintain normal calcium intake.

name: Hypercalcemia (Severe / of Malignancy)
treatment: Aggressive IV hydration, antiresorptive therapy, calcitonin for rapid effect, dialysis in renal failure; treat underlying malignancy.
medications: Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV over 15 min (renal-adjusted)
precautions: Bisphosphonates → osteonecrosis of jaw, nephrotoxicity, hypocalcemia (denosumab especially). Avoid thiazides.

name: Hypocalcemia / Hypoparathyroidism
treatment: Symptomatic/severe (Ca <7.5 mg/dL, tetany, seizure, QT prolonged): IV calcium; chronic: oral calcium + active vitamin D; correct magnesium.
medications: Calcium gluconate 10% 10–20 mL IV over 10 min then infusion
Calcium carbonate 1–2 g elemental/day in divided doses
precautions: Calcium gluconate preferred over chloride peripherally (extravasation necrosis). Avoid hypercalciuria (stones) — target low-normal calcium.

name: Vitamin D Deficiency & Osteomalacia / Rickets
treatment: Vitamin D repletion + adequate calcium; sunlight; treat malabsorption.
medications: Cholecalciferol 60,000 IU weekly × 8 weeks then monthly (India common regimen) or 1,000–4,000 IU daily
children with rickets: 2,000 IU/day × 3 months or stoss therapy 100,000–300,000 IU.
precautions: Avoid mega-doses (>600,000 IU) — hypercalcemia. Monitor calcium in granulomatous disease.

name: Osteoporosis
treatment: Calcium and vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, fall prevention, smoking/alcohol cessation; pharmacotherapy for T-score ≤−2.5, fragility fracture, or high FRAX risk; anabolic first for very high risk.
medications: Alendronate 70 mg weekly, Risedronate 35 mg weekly, Zoledronic acid 5 mg IV yearly
Teriparatide 20 mcg SC daily (max 2 years) or Abaloparatide
precautions: Bisphosphonates: take fasting with full glass of water, stay upright 30 min; avoid if eGFR <30–35; dental check (ONJ); atypical femoral fractures (drug holiday after 5 years oral/3 years IV). Never stop denosumab abruptly without follow-on bisphosphonate (rebound vertebral fractures). Romosozumab → avoid with recent MI/stroke.

name: Paget's Disease of Bone
treatment: Bisphosphonate for bone pain, high ALP, skeletal sites at risk, pre-surgery; analgesics; orthopaedic surgery for complications.
medications: Zoledronic acid 5 mg IV single infusion
precautions: Correct vitamin D before zoledronate (hypocalcemia). Watch sarcomatous change (new pain).

name: Cushing's Syndrome
treatment: Surgical removal of cause (transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenoma, adrenalectomy); medical therapy if surgery fails/not possible; radiotherapy; bilateral adrenalectomy; taper exogenous steroids.
investigations: 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test (cortisol >1.8 mcg/dL abnormal)
precautions: Steroid withdrawal adrenal insufficiency post-cure. High VTE and infection risk (PJP prophylaxis in severe hypercortisolism).

name: Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's Disease)
treatment: Glucocorticoid + mineralocorticoid replacement; sick-day rules (double/triple dose in illness); emergency injection kit; medical alert.
medications: Hydrocortisone 15–25 mg/day in 2–3 doses (e.g., 10-5-5 mg) or Prednisolone 3–5 mg OD
investigations: short Synacthen test (250 mcg; cortisol <18 mcg/dL at 30/60 min)
precautions: Never stop steroids abruptly. Increase dose for surgery/illness. Vomiting → IM/IV hydrocortisone.

name: Adrenal Crisis
treatment: Medical emergency — immediate IV hydrocortisone (don't wait for test results), rapid fluid resuscitation, glucose, treat precipitant.
medications: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV/IM stat, then 50 mg q6h or 200 mg/24 h infusion
Dextrose if hypoglycemic. (Dexamethasone 4 mg if testing needed first — doesn't interfere with cortisol assay.)
investigations: Draw cortisol and ACTH before steroid if possible (without delay)
precautions: High mortality if missed — empirical treatment in hypotensive patients on chronic steroids.

name: Primary Aldosteronism (Conn's Syndrome)
treatment: Unilateral adenoma → laparoscopic adrenalectomy; bilateral hyperplasia → mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.
investigations: Aldosterone-renin ratio (screen all resistant hypertension, hypokalemia, adrenal incidentaloma with HTN — 2025 AHA/ACC)
precautions: Correct hypokalemia before ARR; stop interfering drugs (MRA, diuretics) if feasible. Spironolactone → gynecomastia (eplerenone alternative); hyperkalemia.

name: Pheochromocytoma / Paraganglioma
treatment: Pre-operative alpha-blockade (10–14 days) then beta-blockade, high-salt diet and fluids; laparoscopic adrenalectomy; genetic testing.
medications: Phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BD titrated or Doxazosin 2–16 mg/day
investigations: Plasma free metanephrines or 24-h urine fractionated metanephrines
germline genetic testing (VHL, RET, SDHx, NF1).
precautions: Never start beta-blocker before alpha-blocker (unopposed alpha → hypertensive crisis). Avoid metoclopramide, glucagon, some anesthetics.

name: Prolactinoma / Hyperprolactinemia
treatment: Dopamine agonists first line (even for macroadenomas); surgery for intolerance/resistance; withdraw causative drugs.
medications: Cabergoline 0.25–0.5 mg twice weekly (titrate up to 2 mg/week)
investigations: Serum prolactin (repeat; dilution for hook effect in large tumours)
precautions: High-dose cabergoline → valvulopathy (echo if long-term high dose); impulse control disorders. Monitor visual fields in pregnancy for macroadenomas.

name: Acromegaly
treatment: Transsphenoidal surgery first line; somatostatin analogs, GH-receptor antagonist; radiotherapy for residual disease; manage comorbidities (diabetes, HTN, OSA, colon polyps).
medications: Octreotide LAR 20–40 mg IM monthly or Lanreotide 60–120 mg deep SC monthly
precautions: Somatostatin analogs → gallstones, glucose changes. Monitor LFT on pegvisomant.

name: Hypopituitarism
treatment: Replace deficient hormones; glucocorticoid first before thyroxine; treat cause (tumour, Sheehan's).
