medications: Levothyroxine (titrate to free T4, not TSH)
precautions: Thyroxine before steroid can precipitate adrenal crisis. Steroid sick-day rules.

name: Diabetes Insipidus (Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency/Resistance)
treatment: Central (AVP deficiency): desmopressin. Nephrogenic (AVP resistance): treat cause, low-salt low-protein diet, thiazides, NSAIDs; stop lithium if possible.
medications: Desmopressin 100–200 mcg oral BD–TDS, 10–20 mcg intranasal, or 1–2 mcg SC/IV
investigations: water deprivation test with desmopressin challenge
precautions: Desmopressin → hyponatremia (allow daily breakthrough polyuria, monitor Na). Ensure free access to water.

name: Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
treatment: Treat cause (malignancy, CNS disease, pulmonary disease, drugs); fluid restriction <800–1000 mL/day; salt tablets/urea; hypertonic saline if severe.
medications: Tolvaptan 15–60 mg OD (hospital initiation, limited duration)
precautions: Avoid overcorrection. Tolvaptan → liver injury; avoid in liver disease.

name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
treatment: Glucocorticoid ± mineralocorticoid replacement; salt supplementation in infants; surgical genital reconstruction (shared decision); stress dosing; Crinecerfont as adjunct.
precautions: Salt-wasting crisis in neonates (2–3 weeks). Over-treatment → growth suppression, Cushingoid features.

name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
treatment: Lifestyle and 5–10% weight loss; manage menstrual irregularity, hirsutism, infertility, metabolic risk.
medications: Combined oral contraceptive (e.g., Ethinyl estradiol + Drospirenone/Cyproterone)
Spironolactone 50–100 mg BD (with contraception) for hirsutism
Letrozole 2.5–7.5 mg days 3–7 for ovulation induction (first line)
investigations: Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: oligo-anovulation, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on USG or AMH)
precautions: Spironolactone teratogenic. Endometrial protection if amenorrheic >3 months. Screen for diabetes, depression, OSA.

name: Male Hypogonadism
treatment: Testosterone replacement if symptomatic with consistently low morning testosterone; gonadotropins if fertility desired; treat cause (obesity, opioids, pituitary disease).
medications: Testosterone enanthate/cypionate 100–200 mg IM every 1–2 weeks
Testosterone undecanoate 1000 mg IM every 10–14 weeks
precautions: Testosterone suppresses spermatogenesis (avoid if fertility desired). Monitor hematocrit (stop >54%), PSA. Contraindicated in prostate/breast cancer.

name: Gout (Acute & Chronic)
treatment: Acute flare: NSAID, colchicine or steroids within 24 h; continue urate-lowering therapy during flare. Chronic: treat-to-target serum urate <6 mg/dL (<5 with tophi); lifestyle (reduce alcohol, fructose drinks, red meat/seafood, weight loss).
medications: Acute: Naproxen 500 mg BD, Colchicine 1 mg then 0.5 mg after 1 h (then 0.5 mg BD–TDS), Prednisolone 30–35 mg × 5 days, intra-articular steroid. ULT: Allopurinol start 50–100 mg OD, titrate by 100 mg every 2–4 weeks (up to 800–900 mg)
flare prophylaxis Colchicine 0.5 mg OD for 3–6 months
investigations: serum urate (may be normal in flare — recheck after 2 weeks)
precautions: HLA-B*5801 testing before allopurinol in Han Chinese, Thai, Korean, and consider in South Asian/African ancestry (SJS/TEN risk). Colchicine toxicity with clarithromycin, statins, renal impairment. Febuxostat → CV death warning. Avoid starting ULT without flare prophylaxis.

name: Hyperuricemia (Asymptomatic) & Tumour Lysis Syndrome
treatment: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia — generally no drug therapy; lifestyle. TLS prevention: hydration, allopurinol or rasburicase in high-risk chemotherapy; dialysis for refractory.
medications: Allopurinol 100–300 mg/day (TLS prophylaxis up to 600 mg/day)
precautions: Rasburicase contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis, methemoglobinemia) — test first. Urinary alkalinization no longer recommended.

name: Porphyria (Acute Intermittent Porphyria)
treatment: Stop precipitating drugs, carbohydrate loading, IV hemin, analgesia, treat hyponatremia/seizures; givosiran for recurrent attacks.
precautions: Check drug safety database (drugs-porphyria.org) — avoid barbiturates, sulfonamides, phenytoin, carbamazepine, alcohol, OCPs, fasting. --- # 6. Hematology & Oncology

name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
treatment: Oral iron (alternate-day dosing improves absorption) for 3 months after Hb normalizes; IV iron if intolerance, malabsorption, CKD, heart failure, pregnancy third trimester or severe anemia; find and treat source of loss.
medications: Ferrous sulfate 200 mg (65 mg elemental) OD or alternate days
IV Ferric carboxymaltose 1000 mg (max 20 mg/kg) or Iron sucrose 200 mg × 5 doses
investigations: endoscopy/colonoscopy in men and post-menopausal women
precautions: Oral iron → GI upset, black stools; separate from tea, calcium, PPIs. Ferric carboxymaltose → hypophosphatemia. IV iron anaphylaxis rare — observe 30 min.

name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency / Pernicious Anemia
treatment: Parenteral B12 if neurological involvement or pernicious anemia; high-dose oral B12 effective otherwise; treat cause.
medications: Hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM 3×/week × 2 weeks (neuro: alternate days until no improvement) then every 2–3 months
investigations: anti-intrinsic factor and anti-parietal cell antibodies
precautions: Do not give folate alone in B12 deficiency (neurological damage progresses). Watch hypokalemia early in treatment. Metformin and PPIs cause B12 deficiency.

name: Folate Deficiency Anemia
treatment: Folic acid replacement, improve diet, treat cause; check and correct B12 first.
medications: maintenance 5 mg weekly–daily for chronic hemolysis
precautions: Always exclude B12 deficiency before folate monotherapy.

name: Anemia of Chronic Disease / Inflammation
treatment: Treat underlying condition; IV iron if absolute deficiency coexists; ESA in CKD/chemotherapy; transfuse if symptomatic.
precautions: Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant — interpret with CRP.

name: Beta-Thalassemia Major
treatment: Regular transfusions (keep pre-transfusion Hb 9–10.5 g/dL), iron chelation, splenectomy selectively, hematopoietic stem cell transplant (curative), gene therapy; luspatercept to reduce transfusion burden.
medications: Deferoxamine 20–40 mg/kg SC over 8–12 h 5–7 nights/week
precautions: Iron overload → cardiomyopathy, endocrinopathy, cirrhosis. Deferiprone → agranulocytosis (weekly CBC). Deferasirox → renal/hepatic toxicity. Carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis (India high prevalence).

name: Thalassemia Trait (Minor)
treatment: No treatment; genetic counselling; avoid unnecessary iron.
precautions: Partner screening before pregnancy. Do not give iron unless deficiency proven.

name: Sickle Cell Disease
treatment: Hydroxyurea for all eligible (from 9 months of age), penicillin prophylaxis to age 5, vaccinations, folic acid, transfusions (stroke prevention by TCD), pain crisis management, HSCT/gene therapy.
medications: Penicillin V 125 mg BD (<3 years) / 250 mg BD
precautions: Acute chest syndrome, stroke, splenic sequestration, priapism are emergencies. Avoid dehydration, cold, hypoxia, high altitude. Hydroxyurea teratogenic — monitor CBC.

name: G6PD Deficiency
treatment: Avoid oxidant triggers; supportive care and transfusion for acute hemolysis; phototherapy/exchange transfusion for neonatal jaundice.
medications: avoid Primaquine (except per G6PD-guided dosing), Dapsone, Rasburicase, Nitrofurantoin, Methylene blue, sulfonamides, fava beans.
investigations: G6PD quantitative assay (falsely normal during acute hemolysis — retest 2–3 months)
precautions: Test G6PD before primaquine/tafenoquine for P. vivax radical cure.

name: Hereditary Spherocytosis
treatment: Folic acid; transfusion for aplastic/hemolytic crises; splenectomy (partial/total) for moderate–severe disease after age 6; cholecystectomy if gallstones.
precautions: Parvovirus B19 → aplastic crisis. Overwhelming post-splenectomy infection risk — urgent antibiotics for fever.

name: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (Warm)
treatment: Steroids first line; rituximab second line; transfuse if severe (least incompatible blood); treat cause (lymphoma, CLL, SLE, drugs); splenectomy for refractory.
precautions: Folic acid during hemolysis; VTE prophylaxis (high risk). PJP prophylaxis on prolonged steroids.

name: Aplastic Anemia
treatment: HSCT for young with matched sibling donor; otherwise immunosuppressive therapy with eltrombopag; supportive transfusions (irradiated, leukodepleted), infection prophylaxis.
medications: Horse antithymocyte globulin 40 mg/kg/day × 4 days + Cyclosporine 5 mg/kg/day + Eltrombopag 150 mg OD
precautions: Minimize transfusions before transplant (alloimmunization). Avoid IM injections, NSAIDs.

name: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
treatment: Treat if platelets <30,000/µL or bleeding; steroids first line; IVIG for rapid rise; TPO receptor agonists, rituximab, fostamatinib, splenectomy for chronic ITP; children usually observe.
medications: Dexamethasone 40 mg OD × 4 days (1–3 cycles) or Prednisolone 1 mg/kg × 2–3 weeks tapered
investigations: bone marrow if atypical or age >60.
precautions: Avoid antiplatelets/NSAIDs, IM injections, contact sports. Eltrombopag → hepatotoxicity, take away from dairy/antacids.

name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
treatment: Hematological emergency — daily plasma exchange, steroids, caplacizumab, rituximab; platelet transfusion contraindicated unless life-threatening bleeding.
medications: Therapeutic plasma exchange (1–1.5 plasma volumes daily)
Methylprednisolone 1 g IV × 3 days or Prednisolone 1 mg/kg
Caplacizumab 10 mg IV then 10 mg SC daily
precautions: Start plasma exchange before ADAMTS13 result if PLASMIC score high. Caplacizumab → bleeding.

name: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome
treatment: STEC-HUS: supportive (fluids, dialysis, transfusion), no antibiotics/antimotility. Atypical HUS: complement inhibitor.
medications: Eculizumab 900 mg IV weekly × 4 then 1200 mg q2w or Ravulizumab
precautions: Complement inhibitors → meningococcal infection risk. Antibiotics in STEC may increase HUS risk.

name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
treatment: Treat underlying cause (sepsis, obstetric, trauma, malignancy, APL); supportive blood products if bleeding or procedure planned; anticoagulation if thrombosis predominant.
precautions: Avoid tranexamic acid in DIC (except hyperfibrinolytic states such as APL/prostate cancer under specialist).

name: Hemophilia A & B
treatment: Prophylactic factor replacement or non-factor therapy; on-demand treatment for bleeds; RICE for joint bleeds; physiotherapy; gene therapy.
medications: Factor VIII concentrate (A) or Factor IX (B) — 1 IU/kg FVIII raises level ~2%
Emicizumab 3 mg/kg weekly × 4 then 1.5 mg/kg weekly (Hemophilia A)
Desmopressin 0.3 mcg/kg for mild hemophilia A
precautions: No IM injections, aspirin or NSAIDs. aPCC + emicizumab → thrombotic microangiopathy risk. Treat head injury aggressively.

name: Von Willebrand Disease
treatment: Desmopressin for type 1; vWF-containing concentrates for type 2/3 or surgery; antifibrinolytics for mucosal bleeding; hormonal therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding.
medications: Desmopressin 0.3 mcg/kg IV/SC or 300 mcg intranasal
precautions: Desmopressin → hyponatremia (fluid restriction), tachyphylaxis; contraindicated in type 2B (thrombocytopenia). Avoid NSAIDs.

name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)
treatment: Stop all heparin (including flushes) immediately; start non-heparin anticoagulant; anticoagulate 4 weeks (isolated) to 3 months (with thrombosis).
medications: Warfarin only after platelets recover >150,000 with overlap.
precautions: Do not give platelet transfusion routinely. Avoid warfarin initially (venous limb gangrene). Document as heparin allergy.

name: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
treatment: Thrombotic APS: long-term warfarin (INR 2–3); obstetric APS: aspirin + prophylactic LMWH; catastrophic APS: anticoagulation + steroids + plasma exchange/IVIG.
medications: Enoxaparin 40 mg SC OD in pregnancy (therapeutic if prior thrombosis)
investigations: anti-β2 glycoprotein I IgG/IgM — positive twice 12 weeks apart
precautions: DOACs not recommended, especially in triple-positive/arterial APS (excess thrombosis). Avoid estrogen contraception.

name: Polycythemia Vera
treatment: Phlebotomy to hematocrit <45%, low-dose aspirin; cytoreduction for high-risk (age ≥60 or prior thrombosis); manage CV risk factors.
differential_diagnoses: Secondary polycythemia (hypoxia, COPD, OSA, smoking, high altitude, EPO-secreting tumours, testosterone)
precautions: Hydroxyurea → skin cancers, leg ulcers, teratogenic. Aquagenic pruritus management. Thrombosis risk perioperatively.

name: Essential Thrombocythemia
treatment: Risk-stratified: aspirin for most (low-risk JAK2+); cytoreduction for high-risk (age >60, thrombosis history).
differential_diagnoses: Reactive thrombocytosis (iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, post-splenectomy, malignancy)
precautions: Extreme thrombocytosis (>1.5 million) → acquired vWD — check vWF activity before aspirin.

name: Myelofibrosis
treatment: Risk-stratified (DIPSS/MIPSS70); JAK inhibitors for symptoms/splenomegaly; allogeneic HSCT for high risk (only curative); transfusion support for anemia.
precautions: Ruxolitinib withdrawal syndrome — taper; infection risk (herpes zoster, TB reactivation); Fedratinib → Wernicke encephalopathy (check thiamine).

name: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
treatment: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor for life (or treatment-free remission after deep sustained molecular response ≥2 years); monitor BCR-ABL by qPCR; HSCT for resistance/blast crisis.
medications: Asciminib 80 mg OD (first line or after ≥2 TKIs)
investigations: bone marrow with cytogenetics (Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22))
precautions: Dasatinib → pleural effusion; Nilotinib → QT prolongation, hyperglycemia, PAD; Ponatinib → arterial occlusion; many CYP3A4 interactions. Imatinib pregnancy contraindicated.

name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
treatment: Watch-and-wait for early asymptomatic; treat active disease (iwCLL criteria) with targeted agents; time-limited venetoclax combinations or continuous BTK inhibitor.
medications: Acalabrutinib 100 mg BD or Zanubrutinib 160 mg BD or Ibrutinib 420 mg OD
precautions: Venetoclax → tumour lysis (hydration, allopurinol, ramp-up dosing). BTK inhibitors → AF, bleeding, hypertension. Vaccinate (no live vaccines). Autoimmune cytopenias.

name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
treatment: Fit patients: intensive induction (7+3) ± targeted agents, consolidation (high-dose cytarabine) or allogeneic HSCT by risk. Unfit/elderly: Azacitidine + Venetoclax. APL: ATRA + Arsenic trioxide (emergency).
medications: Cytarabine 100–200 mg/m²/day × 7 days + Daunorubicin 60–90 mg/m² × 3 days
Revumenib/Ziftomenib (menin inhibitors, KMT2A/NPM1). APL: ATRA 45 mg/m²/day + Arsenic trioxide 0.15 mg/kg/day.
precautions: APL: start ATRA on suspicion; differentiation syndrome (dexamethasone); DIC. Tumour lysis prophylaxis. Febrile neutropenia = emergency. Irradiated blood products.

name: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
treatment: Multi-agent induction, consolidation, CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal therapy), maintenance (2–3 years); Ph+ ALL: TKI added; immunotherapy/CAR-T for relapse/MRD+; HSCT for high risk.
precautions: Vincristine is fatal intrathecally — IV only. Asparaginase → pancreatitis, thrombosis, hypersensitivity. Tumour lysis. 6-MP dosing by TPMT/NUDT15.

name: Hodgkin Lymphoma
treatment: Early stage: ABVD × 2–4 ± involved-site radiotherapy (PET-adapted). Advanced: Nivolumab-AVD (2024 data) or BV-AVD, or escalated BEACOPDac; relapse: salvage + autologous transplant.
investigations: Excisional lymph node biopsy (Reed–Sternberg cells, CD15+, CD30+)
precautions: Bleomycin → pulmonary toxicity (avoid high FiO₂). Doxorubicin → cardiotoxicity. Long-term risk of secondary cancers and CVD; breast screening after mediastinal RT.

name: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
treatment: Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP × 6 cycles; CNS prophylaxis for high CNS-IPI; relapse: CAR-T (second line for early relapse), bispecific antibodies, salvage + autologous HSCT.
medications: Rituximab 375 mg/m² + Cyclophosphamide + Doxorubicin + Vincristine + Prednisolone
precautions: HBV reactivation with rituximab — prophylaxis. Tumour lysis. CAR-T → cytokine release syndrome and ICANS.

name: Follicular Lymphoma
treatment: Low tumour burden: watch-and-wait or rituximab monotherapy. High burden: chemoimmunotherapy then maintenance; localized: radiotherapy; relapse: bispecifics, CAR-T.
precautions: Bendamustine → prolonged lymphopenia (PJP/zoster prophylaxis).

name: Multiple Myeloma
treatment: Transplant-eligible: quadruplet induction then autologous HSCT then lenalidomide maintenance. Ineligible: Daratumumab-Lenalidomide-Dexamethasone. Relapse: CAR-T, bispecifics. Bone protection; manage hypercalcemia, renal failure, infections.
precautions: Bortezomib → neuropathy, zoster (acyclovir). Lenalidomide → VTE, teratogenic (REMS). Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast where possible (renal). Daratumumab interferes with crossmatching — type blood before.

name: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS)
treatment: Observation; risk-stratified monitoring (annual for intermediate/high risk); treat related bone disease.
precautions: Annual follow-up; ~1% per year progression risk.

name: Myelodysplastic Syndromes
treatment: Lower-risk: supportive (transfusions, ESA, luspatercept, imetelstat, lenalidomide for del5q). Higher-risk: hypomethylating agents; allogeneic HSCT if fit.
investigations: bone marrow with cytogenetics and molecular panel (SF3B1, TP53)
precautions: Infection and bleeding risk; iron overload in transfused patients.

name: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
treatment: Urgent immunosuppression and treat trigger (infection, malignancy, autoimmune); HSCT for familial/refractory.
precautions: High mortality — don't delay treatment awaiting all criteria. Infection prophylaxis.

name: Breast Cancer
treatment: Multimodal by stage and receptor status (ER/PR/HER2): surgery (breast-conserving/mastectomy + sentinel node), radiotherapy, endocrine therapy, chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, immunotherapy for TNBC; CDK4/6 inhibitors in high-risk/metastatic HR+.
medications: Tamoxifen 20 mg OD (premenopausal) or Letrozole 2.5 mg/Anastrozole 1 mg OD (postmenopausal) × 5–10 years
investigations: staging CT/bone scan/PET for stage III–IV
precautions: Tamoxifen → VTE, endometrial cancer (report bleeding); aromatase inhibitors → bone loss (DEXA, bisphosphonate); trastuzumab → cardiotoxicity (echo q3 months); avoid lymphedema arm injury.

name: Cervical Cancer
treatment: Early stage: radical hysterectomy or fertility-sparing trachelectomy; locally advanced: concurrent chemoradiation (cisplatin) + brachytherapy ± Pembrolizumab; metastatic: chemotherapy + bevacizumab + pembrolizumab. Prevention: HPV vaccination and screening.
precautions: HPV vaccine 9–14 years (single/two-dose schedules per WHO). Radiation proctitis/cystitis. Screen women 30–65 with HPV test every 5 years.

name: Ovarian Cancer
treatment: Cytoreductive surgery (primary or interval after neoadjuvant chemo) + carboplatin/paclitaxel; maintenance PARP inhibitor (BRCA/HRD) ± bevacizumab.
medications: Olaparib 300 mg BD or Niraparib maintenance
precautions: PARP inhibitors → myelosuppression, MDS/AML risk. Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy for BRCA carriers.

name: Endometrial Cancer
treatment: Total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy + sentinel node; adjuvant radiotherapy/chemotherapy by molecular risk; advanced: chemo-immunotherapy; progestins for fertility-sparing atypical hyperplasia/early grade 1.
medications: Carboplatin + Paclitaxel + Dostarlimab or Pembrolizumab (dMMR especially)
